# Realot Studio documentation

> Source-aligned documentation for Realot Studio: editor workflows, scripting API, components, physics, navigation and export.

> **What is Realot Studio?:** A browser-based 2D game engine with a visual editor, JavaScript gameplay scripting, PixiJS rendering and Rapier2D physics. The hosted engine is updated by publishing its web files; users do not need a separate engine installer.

## Start here

[**Transform**Position, rotation and scale. Every spatial entity uses a Transform.](api/components/transform.html)[**SpriteRenderer**Draw a 2D texture sprite for an entity.](api/components/spriterenderer.html)[**ShapeRenderer**Draw a procedural 2D shape without requiring a sprite asset.](api/components/shaperenderer.html)[**TextRenderer**Render text either in world space or as screen-space UI.](api/components/textrenderer.html)[**StrokePath**A variable-thickness strip along placed points — rivers, cables, roads, conveyor belts or walls — with flat color or…](api/components/strokepath.html)[**SpeechBubble**Speech bubble UI attached to an entity, useful for dialogue and NPC callouts.](api/components/speechbubble.html)[**ChatLog**Scrollable-style conversation log component for UI dialogue.](api/components/chatlog.html)[**TextInput**Interactive text input control driven by the runtime UI system.](api/components/textinput.html)[**Joystick**Virtual touch joystick for mobile and pointer-driven control schemes.](api/components/joystick.html)[**Rigidbody2D**2D physics body backed by the engine physics runtime. Dynamic, Kinematic and Static bodies have different script…](api/components/rigidbody2d.html)[**Collider2D**Physics collision shape and contact filtering. A Collider2D is also required for accurate pointer/touch hit tests.](api/components/collider2d.html)[**Joint2D**Connect physics bodies with Fixed, Revolute, Prismatic, Rope or Spring constraints.](api/components/joint2d.html)[**CharacterController**High-level movement modes: Character Controller, Platformer, Top-Down, Car, Follow, Patrol and Free.](api/components/charactercontroller.html)[**SpriteAnimation**Sprite-sheet/clip animation state on a SpriteRenderer.](api/components/spriteanimation.html)[**Camera**Orthographic 2D camera with reference resolutions, responsive scaling, follow, shake and optional pseudo-3D sprite…](api/components/camera.html)[**AudioSource**Play a local audio asset, optionally with distance-based 3D attenuation.](api/components/audiosource.html)[**AudioListener**Defines the hearing area for 3D audio and drives audio enter/leave callbacks.](api/components/audiolistener.html)[**Light**2D light source supporting Directional, Point, Spot, Area, GodRays and Freeform light shapes.](api/components/light.html)[**ShadowCaster**Marks an entity as a shadow occluder for the lighting system.](api/components/shadowcaster.html)[**LightingSettings**Scene-wide lighting quality and mood controls. Attach to one entity; the lighting system reads it scene-wide.](api/components/lightingsettings.html)[**NavAgent2D**Per-agent navigation settings and current path state for NavWorld2D pathfinding.](api/components/navagent2d.html)[**NavWorld2D**Shared navigation world for baked or dynamic 2D pathfinding, with 16 navigation areas.](api/components/navworld2d.html)[**Tileset**Defines a reusable 16-role autotile set. The editor can auto-slice one image or accept separate role images.](api/components/tileset.html)[**Tilemap**Sparse painted tile grid that references a Tileset entity by ID.](api/components/tilemap.html)[**Script**Script component holding a script name, source and enabled state.](api/components/script.html)

# Realot Studio documentation

> Source-aligned documentation for Realot Studio: editor workflows, scripting API, components, physics, navigation and export.

> **What is Realot Studio?:** A browser-based 2D game engine with a visual editor, JavaScript gameplay scripting, PixiJS rendering and Rapier2D physics. The hosted engine is updated by publishing its web files; users do not need a separate engine installer.

<!-- page: docs/getting-started/installation.html -->
# Use Realot Studio

> Realot Studio is a browser-based engine. Open the hosted site; local hosting is optional.

## Normal use: open the website

> **No engine installer is required:** Realot Studio runs as a browser application. Open the hosted Realot site in a modern browser and use the Hub to create or open a project. The editor and runtime are delivered as web files; you do not need to download a separate engine installer to use the hosted version.

When the engine owner publishes an update to the hosted site, the new files are available from the same website address. A normal page reload while online retrieves the published files. A previously installed PWA can continue using cached assets offline until it reconnects and refreshes.

## Optional browser installation

On a supported browser and deployment, choose the Hub's **Install app** action or use the browser's own install option. This adds an app-like launcher entry. It is still the same web application and does not create a separate downloadable engine release.

## Optional: host the engine yourself

The supplied engine project is a static web application. To preview a local copy or publish your own deployment, serve the project folder over HTTP(S). For a quick local preview, run this command from the folder containing the engine files:

```
python3 -m http.server 5000
```

Then open `http://localhost:5000/`. Do not open the main HTML file directly with `file://`; browser module, fetch and WebAssembly loading require an HTTP origin.

## Browser requirements

- A modern browser with JavaScript modules and WebAssembly.
- Canvas/WebGL support for the renderer.
- Browser storage for project data and preferences.
- HTTPS for production deployments that need secure browser APIs or PWA installation (localhost is treated as secure for development).

## Android APK export

Android APK export is separate from normal browser use. Realot packages the game in the browser and sends the standalone web export to the configured Android build service. The editor does not run Android Studio, Gradle or an Android SDK locally. See [Android APK export](../export/android.html) for the current workflow.


---

<!-- page: docs/getting-started/hub.html -->
# The Realot Hub

> Use Projects to create and reopen games, and Learn to open the built-in guide.

## Overview

The Hub is the Realot Studio home screen. It is the starting point for opening projects, creating a new game from a template, and opening the built-in learning material. The current Hub has two views: **Projects** and **Learn**.

| View | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Projects | Shows your saved project cards. Start with a template, create a blank project, search/sort your projects, switch between grid and list layouts, or reopen a recent project. |
| Learn | Opens the Hub's learning area. The built-in quick guide is part of the engine distribution and can be cached for offline access. |

## Starter templates

The current template gallery includes:

| Template | Starting point |
| --- | --- |
| Blank Canvas | An empty project for custom 2D scenes and logic. |
| Platformer Kit | A platformer starter with a kinematic character controller and one-way platforms. |
| Top-Down | A top-down starter with a player, NPCs, collectibles and a dungeon scene. |
| Flappy Bird | A flap-to-fly starter with scoring and a simple game-state flow. |
| Sky Jumper | An endless jumping starter with platforms, stars and a following camera. |
| Physics Sandbox | A scene for experimenting with Rapier2D bodies, colliders and joints. |

## Install the Hub as an app

Realot is a web application. On browsers and deployments that support installation, the title bar can show an **Install app** action when the browser confirms the site is installable. Installation creates an app-like shortcut; it does not download a separate engine release. The service worker can cache the Hub, editor and runtime for supported offline use.

Updates are published to the hosted site. When the browser is online, reload the site to receive the current published files. An installed PWA may continue using cached files while offline and will need to reconnect to refresh them.

## Project files

**File → Save Project** downloads your project as a `.realot` file. This is Realot Studio's portable project format and includes the scenes, assets, prefabs, tags, navigation-area names and scripts needed to continue editing the game.

**Open a project from your computer:** install Realot Hub as a PWA in a supported desktop browser. Then double-click a downloaded `.realot` file in your file manager. The operating system opens the installed Realot app, and Realot loads that project in the editor. When asked, you can allow Realot to keep saving changes back to that same file. This file-opening behavior requires an installed PWA and browser/operating-system support for web-app file handling; if that option is unavailable, open the editor and use **File → Load Project**.

<!-- page: docs/getting-started/first-game.html -->
# Build your first game

> A practical first-game path using entities, components and a simple script.

## 1. Start with a scene

Create a scene and add an entity. The editor stores scene state as JSON-compatible data: entities have IDs, names, tags, active state, optional hierarchy folders/prefab metadata, and a component map.

## 2. Add a visual

Attach a `SpriteRenderer` and assign a sprite asset, or use a `ShapeRenderer` when you want a procedural primitive. Add a `Camera` and mark one camera as the main camera.

## 3. Add physics when you need it

A typical physics actor uses a `Rigidbody2D` plus a `Collider2D`. Choose Dynamic, Kinematic or Static based on who is responsible for movement.

## 4. Add a Script component

Put a script on the entity and define lifecycle functions. Realot Studio calls `onStart()` once and `onUpdate(dt)` every render frame.

```
function onStart() {
  this.speed = 220;
}

function onUpdate(dt) {
  if (input.keyDown("ArrowRight")) {
    this.x += this.speed * dt;
  }
  if (input.keyDown("ArrowLeft")) {
    this.x -= this.speed * dt;
  }
}
```

## 5. Prefer frame-rate-independent movement

Use `time.deltaTime` (or the `dt` lifecycle argument) when movement is expressed in units per second. Keep physics-step work in `onFixedUpdate(dt)` when the logic should track the fixed simulation cadence.

## 6. Run, iterate, export

Use the editor’s Play flow to test, inspect the Debug HUD when diagnosing runtime behavior, then use **Export** for HTML5, PWA or Android APK.


---

<!-- page: docs/getting-started/scripting.html -->
# Scripting quickstart

> Learn the Realot Studio JavaScript scripting model in one page.

## Script shape

Realot Studio scripts are plain JavaScript functions executed by the ScriptSystem. You do not create a class instance yourself. The engine binds the entity context to `this`.

```
function onStart() {
  this.health = 100;
}

function onUpdate(dt) {
  this.x += 100 * dt;
}
```

## The two layers of the API

| Layer | Examples | Use when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entity context (`this`) | `this.x`, `this.sprite`, `this.rigidbody`, `this.destroy()` | You are acting on the current entity. |
| Globals | `findFirst()`, `scene.load()`, `physics.raycast()`, `input.keyDown()` | You need scene-wide services or another entity. |

## Common component shortcuts

When a component exists on the entity, the corresponding module is exposed on `this`: `this.sprite`, `this.shape`, `this.text`, `this.rigidbody`, `this.controller`, `this.animator`, `this.camera`, `this.audio`, `this.collider`, `this.joint`, `this.navAgent`, `this.light`, `this.shadowCaster`, `this.strokePath`, and more.

## Discoverability

The editor’s script autocomplete is sourced from the same public API lists documented here. A good rule for generated code is: use documented globals and component modules; do not reach into internal runtime systems or editor modules.


---

<!-- page: docs/concepts/architecture.html -->
# Architecture

> How Realot Studio separates runtime, editor, standalone runtime, components and systems.

## Runtime / editor / target

The distribution follows a hard separation: `project/runtime/` is the engine shipped with games; `project/editor/` is the development tool; `project/player/` is the standalone runtime shell. Runtime must not import editor code; editor may import runtime code.

## Components are data

Components are plain data objects. Rendering, physics, lighting, audio and other behavior live in systems. This keeps scene serialization straightforward and makes the same scene data usable by the editor and standalone runtime.

## Systems run in an explicit order

| Order | System |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | ControllerSystem |
| 2 | PhysicsSystem |
| 3 | AnimationSystem |
| 4 | SpeechBubbleSystem |
| 5 | TextInputSystem |
| 6 | JoystickSystem |
| 7 | AudioSystem |
| 8 | AudioListenerSystem |
| 9 | ScriptSystem |
| 10 | Late controller work |
| 11 | RenderSystem |
| 12 | TilemapSystem |
| 13 | NavWorldSystem |
| 14 | LightingSystem |
| 15 | CameraRenderSystem |

## Rendering containers

The runtime separates game-content rendering, screen-space UI and late letterbox/pillarbox bars. Debug lines render in the world container. This separation explains why screen-space UI components such as TextRenderer can remain fixed while the world camera moves.


---

<!-- page: docs/concepts/entities-components.html -->
# Entities & components

> Understand Realot Studio scene entities, IDs, tags, component composition and runtime cloning.

## Entity identity

An entity has a unique stable ID such as `e12`, a human-facing name, a tag, active state, optional hierarchy folder, prefab metadata and a component map. Names and tags are not unique; IDs are.

## Why IDs matter

Use `findById(id)` when you mean one exact entity. Use name/tag queries when you intentionally want one or many matches. Runtime clones keep unique IDs and expose `isClone`.

## Component composition

A gameplay actor can combine Transform + SpriteRenderer + Collider2D + Rigidbody2D + Script. A UI button might combine Transform + TextRenderer + Collider2D + Script. There is no requirement that every entity have every component.

## Runtime cloning

Use `spawn()` or `this.spawn()` to clone an authored entity. The returned context is the new live entity; `onClone()` runs for runtime clones before `onStart()`.

```
function onUpdate() {
  if (input.keyPressed("Space")) {
    var bullet = spawn("Bullet", { x: this.x, y: this.y });
    bullet.rotation = this.rotation; // configure the clone right after spawning
  }
}

// Inside Bullet’s own script:
function onClone() {
  this.tag = "projectile"; // runs once, before this clone’s onStart()
}
```

## Destroying entities

`this.destroy()` queues destruction for the end of the frame. `onDestroy()` runs before removal. Waiting/repeating timers owned by the entity are automatically cancelled when the entity is destroyed.


---

<!-- page: docs/concepts/game-loop-scenes.html -->
# Game loop & scenes

> Understand frame updates, fixed physics updates and scene transitions.

## Render-frame lifecycle

| Hook | When it runs |
| --- | --- |
| onStart() | Once before the first onUpdate(). |
| onClone() | Once for runtime clones, immediately before onStart(). |
| onUpdate(dt) | Every render frame. |
| onClick() | On the frame a mouse/finger press targets an entity with a collider. |
| onFixedUpdate(dt) | Fixed 60 Hz simulation cadence. |
| onDestroy() | Before the entity is removed or the scene ends. |

## Collision & trigger lifecycle

Use `onCollisionEnter(other)`, `onCollisionStay(other)` and `onCollisionExit(other)` for physical contacts. `onCollision(other)` remains an alias for collision-enter behavior. Trigger-only callbacks are `onTriggerEnter(other)` and `onTriggerExit(other)`.

## Scene controls

Use `scene.current` to read the current scene name, `scene.load(name)` to switch scenes, `scene.restart()` to restart, and `scene.pause()`/`scene.resume()` to freeze gameplay while leaving rendering responsive.

```
function onTriggerEnter(other) {
  if (other.name === "Target") scene.load("Level2");
}

function onUpdate() {
  if (input.keyPressed("Escape")) {
    scene.isPaused ? scene.resume() : scene.pause();
  }
}
```

## Pause semantics

During `scene.pause()`, physics, scripts, animation and audio stop advancing until resume. Rendering stays responsive, which is useful for pause menus and debugging UI.


---

<!-- page: docs/reference/coordinate-system.html -->
# Coordinate system & conventions

> The signs, units, axes, rotation conventions and reference-resolution rules that prevent common Realot Studio scripting mistakes.

> **Core convention:** Realot Studio is a 2D screen-style coordinate system: +X is right and +Y is down. Treat Y signs accordingly when writing movement, offsets, camera/UI positioning, and physics examples.

## Transform axes

| Value | Positive direction | Common use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `x` | Right | Horizontal world movement and placement. |
| `y` | Down | Vertical placement; jumping/falling code should use negative/positive signs according to the movement system being used. |
| `z` | Depth layer / pseudo-3D input | Affects pseudo-3D rendering only when the camera’s pseudo-3D behavior is enabled. |
| `rotation` | Degrees around Z | Used by sprites, lights and directional orientation; 0 points along +X for directional/spot style aiming. |
| `scaleX` / `scaleY` | 1 = native size | Values above 1 enlarge; values below 1 shrink; negative values mirror the axis. |

## UI coordinates

Screen-space Text, TextInput, ChatLog and Joystick components use the reference-resolution pixel convention supplied by the Camera/device-fit pipeline. This is why HUD coordinates remain stable when the physical device resolution changes.

## Angles and vectors

Vector-like APIs use ordinary JavaScript objects such as `{x, y}`. When converting a direction to an angle, remember that the canvas/world Y axis points downward, so visually “up” is negative Y.

## Timing

| Concept | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `time.deltaTime` | Seconds since the previous script update; multiply speeds expressed per second by deltaTime. |
| `wait(seconds,...)` | Wall-clock game/script timer in seconds. |
| `repathInterval` | Navigation re-plan period in seconds. |

<!-- page: docs/editor/overview.html -->
# Editor overview

> Navigate the Realot Studio editor and understand the main development surfaces.

## Main surfaces

| Area | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Hierarchy | Shows entities in the current scene, including hierarchy folders. |
| Inspector | Edits entity metadata and component properties. |
| Viewport | Scene/game editing and gizmos. |
| Script editor | Edit JavaScript with engine-aware autocomplete. |
| Bottom panels | Animation, tileset, navigation, status and related workflows. |
| Toolbar / menus | Save, project I/O, physics layers, navigation areas, entity creation and export. |

## Entity creation

The Add Component workflow exposes the engine’s authoring components, including Rigidbody2D, Collider2D, Joint2D, CharacterController, SpriteRenderer, SpriteAnimation, ShapeRenderer, StrokePath, Light, AudioSource, AudioListener, ShadowCaster, LightingSettings, Tileset, Tilemap, NavWorld2D, NavAgent2D, TextRenderer, SpeechBubble, ChatLog, TextInput and Joystick.

## Editor principle

The editor writes serializable scene/project data. Runtime systems consume that data. Private helper modules under `project/editor/` should be treated as implementation details, not game scripting APIs.

<!-- page: docs/editor/controls.html -->
# Editor controls & exact locations

> Exact Realot Studio UI paths, panel positions, keyboard shortcuts, conditional tools, and where feature-specific buttons live.

> **Navigation rule:** This page is an index, not a substitute for feature docs. Each feature page also states the exact control path needed to perform its workflow.

## Editor layout

| Region | Location | What it contains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Top toolbar | Across the top | File, Edit, GameObject, UI, Window; transform/navigation tools; Play/Pause; Export; Hub. |
| Hierarchy | Left, fixed-width column (~213px) | Current scene entity tree, search, folders, selection and add shortcuts. |
| Viewport | Center | Scene/Game tabs, viewport toolbar, canvas and editor gizmos. |
| Inspector | Right, fixed-width column (~255px) | Selected entity name/tag, components, property fields, Add Component and feature-specific buttons. |
| Bottom panel | Bottom edge | Project and Console tabs; scenes, sprites, audio, scripts, prefabs and runtime/editor logs. |

## Top menu paths

| Path | Open by clicking | Available commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| File | File | Save Now / Saved, Save Project, Optimize Assets on Save, Load Project…, Export…, Extra Backup Storage, Restore from Backup Folder. |
| Edit | Edit | Physics Layers… and Nav Areas…. |
| Window | Window | Hierarchy, Asset Panel and Inspector show/hide checkboxes; Show All Panels while any panel is hidden. See [Editor settings & performance](settings.html). |
| GameObject | GameObject | Empty GameObject, Light, 2D Object, Shape. |
| UI | UI | Text, Speech Bubble, Chat Log, Message Input, Joystick. |
| GameObject → Light | GameObject → Light | Directional Light, Point Light, Spot Light, Area Light, God Rays, Freeform Light. |
| GameObject → 2D Object | GameObject → 2D Object | Tileset, Tilemap, Nav World 2D, Stroke Path. |
| GameObject → Shape | GameObject → Shape | Square, Circle, Capsule, Triangle. |

## Toolbar tools and shortcuts

| Key | Tool | When visible | Exact behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Q | Hand / Pan | Always | Drag to pan; scroll to zoom. |
| W | Translate | Always | Move selected entity with transform gizmo. |
| E | Rotate | Always | Rotate selected entity. |
| R | Scale | Always | Scale selected entity. |
| T | Tile | When a Tilemap or Tileset exists | Paint tile cells. |
| Y | Erase | When a Tilemap or a Nav World 2D exists | Erase tiles / relevant paint data. |
| P | Path | When a Stroke Path exists | Append/move/insert path points. |
| U | Nav paint walkable | When a Nav World 2D exists | Click = walkable; Alt-click = clear override. |
| I | Nav paint blocked | When a Nav World 2D exists | Click = blocked; Alt-click = clear override. |
| O | Nav area paint | When a Nav World 2D exists | Click = assign selected area; Alt-click = clear area. |

## Selection, history and playback shortcuts

These global shortcuts are ignored while you type in a text field, while the Script Editor is open, and while the Export window is open. Ctrl is Cmd on macOS.

| Shortcut | Action | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Delete / Backspace | Delete the selected entities | Requires a selection. |
| Ctrl+C | Copy selection | Yields to normal text copy when text is selected on the page. |
| Ctrl+V | Paste |  |
| Ctrl+D | Duplicate selection | Copy + paste in one step. |
| Ctrl+Z | Undo | Scene edits and Animation-editor edits keep separate histories; undo acts on whichever editor is active. Up to 100 steps. |
| Ctrl+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y | Redo |  |
| Space | Toggle Play | Opens or closes the Play window. |

## Conditional controls

Some controls intentionally do not exist until the related scene object exists. This is important when documenting or generating instructions: do not tell users to click a hidden tool before creating the required object.

| Control | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| Tile (T) | A Tilemap or Tileset exists in the current world. |
| Erase (Y) | A Tilemap or a Nav World 2D exists (a Tileset alone does not enable it). |
| Path (P) | A Stroke Path exists. |
| U / I / O Nav brushes | A Nav World 2D exists. |
| Nav bounds/cells view | A Nav World 2D exists. |
| Paint Area selector | Nav Area tool O is active and named areas exist. |


---

<!-- page: docs/editor/settings.html -->
# Editor settings and configuration

> Complete reference for the editor menus, panel visibility, physics layers, navigation areas, Inspector notes, saving preferences and performance defaults.

## Where the settings are

Realot Studio does not currently have one large Settings window. Options are placed beside the editor feature they control: use **File** for project storage and export, **Edit** for physics and navigation labels, and **Window** for panel visibility. Component-specific settings live in the Inspector and are documented on each [component reference page](../api/index.html).

## File menu

| Menu item | What it does | Availability / notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Save Now / Saved** | Immediately saves the open Hub project to its browser autosave storage. The label shows whether there are unsaved changes. | Shown when the project was opened with a Hub autosave slot. |
| **Save Project** | Downloads a portable `.realot` project archive. When editing a supported file handle, the label can become *Save to [filename]*. | Available for project export to a local file. |
| **Auto-update file: ON / OFF** | Controls whether changes are automatically written back to the opened project file. | Only shown when a supported file handle is active. This is local file writing, not cloud sync. |
| **Save as copy (download)** | Downloads a separate copy without replacing the current file. | Shown when a file handle exists or the browser supports the Save File Picker. |
| **Optimize Assets on Save: ON / OFF** | Arms an optimization pass for the next Save Project operation. When enabled, supported PNG images are losslessly optimized and WAV audio is repacked before the archive is written. | Toggle does not save immediately; the next Save Project action performs the work. |
| **Load Project…** | Opens a saved Realot project file. | Choose a `.realot` project. Loading a project containing scripts asks for confirmation because scripts execute as page code. Loading a project containing scripts asks for confirmation because scripts execute as page code. |
| **Export…** | Opens the standalone game export window. | See [Export window](../export/export-window.html) and [Android APK](../export/android.html). |
| **Enable Extra Backup Storage…** | Lets you select a local folder for mirrored project autosaves, outside the browser's normal storage quota. | Requires browser support for the File System Access API and user permission. |
| **Extra Backup Storage: ON** | Turns off future mirroring to the selected folder. | Does not delete files already written to that folder. |
| **Restore from Backup Folder…** | Restores the most recent project snapshot mirrored to the selected folder. | Only shown while extra backup storage is enabled for the project. |

## Edit menu

| Menu item | What it configures |
| --- | --- |
| **Physics Layers…** | Opens the 16-slot physics layer-name editor. Slot 0 starts as `Default` and cannot be cleared, though it can be renamed. Slots 1–15 can be named or left blank. These names are labels for the fixed runtime layer indices used by Collider2D layer/mask filtering and physics queries. |
| **Nav Areas…** | Opens the 16-slot navigation-area name editor. Slot 0 starts as `Ground` and cannot be cleared; slot 1 starts as `Water`; slots 2–15 are initially blank. Names can be changed or cleared except for slot 0. The slot indices are stored in navigation cells and NavAgent2D area masks. |

Physics-layer and navigation-area names are saved with project data. The indices—not the text labels—are what collision filtering and pathfinding use at runtime. Renaming an existing slot does not move its contents to another index.

## Project tags

Use the selected entity's **Tag** dropdown in the Inspector to assign a tag. The initial list contains `Untagged`, `Player` and `Enemy`. These are ordinary tag names supplied as starting defaults; `Player` and `Enemy` do not have automatic engine behavior just because of their names.

- Choose **Add Tag…** in the dropdown to create a project tag.
- Custom tags can be removed from the tag list. `Untagged` is protected and cannot be deleted.
- `Player` and `Enemy` are not protected; they can be removed like other tags.
- Removing a tag removes it from the dropdown. Entities that already carry that tag keep their current tag value until you change it.
- The available tag list is included in the saved project snapshot. An entity's assigned tag is stored with its scene data.

Tags are separate from physics layers and navigation areas. Use physics layers for collision filtering and navigation areas for pathfinding costs or masks; use tags to identify objects in editor workflows and scripts.

## GameObject and UI menus

**GameObject → Empty GameObject** creates an empty entity. **GameObject → Light** provides Directional, Point, Spot, Area, God Rays and Freeform lights. **GameObject → 2D Object** creates a Tileset, Tilemap, Nav World 2D or Stroke Path. **GameObject → Shape** creates Square, Circle, Capsule or Triangle shapes with a matching visible ShapeRenderer and collider.

The **UI** menu creates a Text object, Speech Bubble, Chat Log, Message Input (TextInput) or Joystick. These are shortcuts for creating an entity with the corresponding component; the full settings are on each component's reference page.

## Window menu and panel visibility

| Panel | What it contains | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Hierarchy** | Scene entities and their selection/order. | Visible |
| **Asset Panel** | Bottom editor area for assets and related project panels. | Visible |
| **Inspector** | Selected entity properties and component settings. | Visible |

Choose a panel name under **Window** to show or hide it. Hiding a panel gives more room to the Scene view. When one or more panels are hidden, **Show All Panels** restores them. Visibility is remembered in this browser, not stored as a project setting.

## Inspector component notes

The Inspector's information toggle controls optional explanatory notes below component settings. It is a display preference; actionable setup warnings remain visible independently. The default is off.

## Performance preferences and defaults

The current source defines the following stored preferences under the browser storage key `realot_engine_settings`. This is a reference to the shipped implementation—not a hidden user settings screen. Apart from the Inspector component-notes toggle described above, the current editor does not expose controls for these performance preferences in a general Settings dialog.

| Stored setting | Default | Meaning / supported values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `editorFpsFocused` | `60` | Target rendering rate for the editor viewport while the editor window is focused. |
| `editorFpsUnfocused` | `24` | Target rendering rate for the editor viewport while unfocused. |
| `gameFps` | `60` | Play-window target: `30`, `60`, `120`, or `0` for unlimited (limited by the browser's animation-frame scheduling). |
| `backgroundRendering` | `true` | Allows throttled editor rendering to continue while the editor is unfocused rather than fully pausing. |
| `vsync` | `true` | Stored vertical-sync preference read by the rendering scheduler. |
| `showComponentNotes` | `false` | Whether optional Inspector component notes are displayed. This one is toggled by the Inspector UI. |

These values are implementation defaults and targets, not guarantees that a browser, device or display can maintain a particular frame rate. The editor viewport's focused/unfocused caps are separate from the runtime frame loop in an exported game.

## Console and diagnostics

The Console is part of the bottom editor area. It displays editor messages and script output; use its **Copy** control to copy visible logs and **Clear** to clear them. The gameplay debug HUD is separate: scripts can enable it with `debug.show()` in the Play window. See [Global API](../scripting/globals.html).

## Component settings

Component-specific options are not centralized in this page. The source-derived [component reference](../api/index.html) lists every public scene field, its data type, current default and script-facing API members for all 25 components. For navigation, physics and animation workflows, start with the corresponding [Physics](physics.html), [Navigation](navigation.html) and [Assets & animation](assets-animation.html) guides.


---

<!-- page: docs/editor/hierarchy-inspector.html -->
# Hierarchy & Inspector

> Organize the current scene and edit entities/components with stable serialized data.

> **Exact control path:** Select the entity in the left Hierarchy panel or click it in the center Scene view. Its properties appear immediately in the right Inspector . The Add Component button is at the bottom of the Inspector’s component list; use its search field to find a component by name.

## Hierarchy

The Hierarchy shows only entities that belong to the active scene. Entities can also belong to hierarchy folders. The saved scene stores folders separately so folder IDs remain stable across save/load.

## Inspector

The Inspector edits the entity name, tag, active state, component properties and component-specific authoring fields. For many components, the Inspector exposes more authoring fields than the runtime script API intentionally does.

## Gizmos and shapes

Spatial editing uses scene-view gizmos for things such as triangle collider/shape points and other editable geometry. Treat these as authoring controls; scripts should use the documented component APIs instead of manipulating editor gizmo state.


---

<!-- page: docs/editor/scenes-projects.html -->
# Scenes & projects

> Save, load, switch, duplicate and serialize Realot Studio scenes and project manifests.

> **Exact control path:** Project-level scene/file operations are in the bottom Project panel. Scene creation uses Project → Scenes → New Scene ; Save Project and Load Project are in the top File menu. The autosave indicator/action is also exposed through File → Save Now / Saved .

## Scene workflow

The Scene Manager supports creating, saving, switching, renaming, duplicating and deleting scenes. The last remaining scene cannot be deleted.

## Project compatibility

The project manifest stores compatibility metadata. When a project created by a newer engine build is opened in an older build, the editor can show a compatibility warning. This information belongs to the saved project and does not create versioned documentation pages or download releases.

## Recommended practice

Keep source projects with explicit scene names, tags and stable IDs. Keep backups of important project archives before opening them in a different engine build, especially when compatibility warnings appear.

## Save and reopen a project

Choose **File → Save Project** in the editor to download a `.realot` project file. To reopen it by double-clicking, install Realot Hub as a PWA in a desktop browser that supports file handling. Double-click the `.realot` file in your file manager; the installed Realot app opens the project in the editor. Realot can ask permission to save future changes back to the same file. If your browser does not support PWA file handling, use **File → Load Project** inside the editor.


---

<!-- page: docs/editor/assets-animation.html -->
# Assets & animation

> Use sprites, animation clips and audio assets from the editor.

> **Exact control path:** Imported sprites/audio/scripts/prefabs live in the bottom Project panel. Drag supported assets into the center Scene viewport. For animation, add Sprite Animation in the Inspector, then use the Animation editor window to create clips and import frames.

## Sprites

SpriteRenderer points at an asset key rather than embedding image data in the component. This keeps scene JSON lightweight and lets exported runtime assets remain separate.

## Animation

SpriteAnimation stores clips and current playback state. Scripts can call `this.animator.play("Run")`, stop playback and inspect current clip/frame information.

## Audio

AudioSource stores the asset key plus playback properties. 3D sources use `minDistance` for full volume and fade toward silence at `maxDistance`. AudioListener defines the hearing radius and sound enter/leave callbacks are available to scripts.


---

<!-- page: docs/editor/prefabs.html -->
# Prefab workflow

> Create, place, edit, update, revert and unpack Realot Studio prefabs with the exact editor controls involved.

> **What a prefab is:** In Realot Studio a prefab is a reusable one-entity template. Instances keep a prefabId and track field-level overrides. Updating a prefab can propagate the canonical data to other instances.

## Create a prefab

Select an entity in the Scene viewport or Hierarchy. In the right Inspector, use the small prefab/box action next to the entity name. The engine creates a prefab from that entity and links the source entity to it.

## Place an instance

Use the bottom Project panel → Prefabs folder. Drag a prefab asset into the center Scene viewport. The editor instantiates the template and places the new instance in the scene.

## Edit an instance

Change component values normally in the Inspector. Realot Studio records changed fields as prefab overrides for that instance.

## Update the prefab

When an instance is selected, the Inspector shows a blue Prefab strip. Optional Update Transform checkboxes control whether Position, Rotation, and Scale should also propagate to other instances. Click Update Prefab to make this instance the new canonical template.

## Revert / Unpack

| Inspector control | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `Revert Prefab` | Discard the instance’s overrides and re-sync its values from the prefab. |
| `Unpack Prefab` | Detach this instance while keeping its current values. Future prefab updates no longer reach it. |

## Delete a prefab asset

Bottom Project → Prefabs. Use the asset delete control. Existing objects keep their current data but are no longer linked to the deleted prefab.

## Important implementation fact

Prefab data is stored in the project’s `prefabs.json` catalogue and is included by Save Project/import/export flows.


---

<!-- page: docs/editor/physics.html -->
# Physics authoring

> Configure rigid bodies, colliders, joints, layers and one-way platforms.

> **Exact control path:** Physics components are added from Inspector → Add Component (Rigidbody 2D, Collider 2D, Joint 2D, Movement Type). Global named physics layer slots are edited at Edit → Physics Layers… .

## Rigid bodies

| Body type | Typical responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Dynamic | Physics solver controls movement; scripts apply forces/impulses or read/write velocity. |
| Kinematic | Scripts/controllers request movement; collision resolution produces contact state. |
| Static | Fixed world geometry; no dynamic motion. |

## Colliders

Collider2D supports Box, Circle, Capsule and Triangle shapes. You can enable triggers, one-way platforms, friction/restitution, density, offsets and 16-layer collision filtering.

## Collision layers

Each collider belongs to one layer (0-15) and exposes a 16-bit mask of layers it can interact with. A raycast can use `physics.layer(…)` to build the same mask model for query filtering.

## Joints

Joint2D supports Fixed, Revolute, Prismatic, Rope and Spring. Rope and Spring use multi-segment chains for visual/physical behavior and expose anchors, length, stiffness/damping and optional motors/limits.

## One-way platforms

> **Direction matters:** A one-way platform is a Collider2D with isOneWayPlatform = true . The physics system distinguishes pass-through movement from the blocking direction, so the behavior should be tested with the body moving from both sides.


---

<!-- page: docs/editor/navigation.html -->
# Navigation authoring

> Bake 2D navigation with NavWorld2D and configure NavAgent2D.

> **Exact control path:** Create the shared nav grid with GameObject → 2D Object → Nav World 2D . Then the top toolbar exposes U walkable, I blocked and O area paint tools. Brush −/+ controls sit directly beside those nav tools. Named areas are configured at Edit → Nav Areas… .

## NavWorld2D

A NavWorld2D defines world bounds, cell size and authored/baked cell data. It supports 16 navigation areas, per-area costs, optional diagonal traversal and optional dynamic rebuilding.

## Agents

NavAgent2D adds radius, speed, acceleration/deceleration, stopping distance, automatic repathing and avoidance. Vehicle-oriented settings are available for car-style navigation/steering.

## Script access

Scripts use the global `nav` module: `nav.findPath()`, `nav.isWalkable()` and `nav.bake()`. A NavAgent exposes its live `currentPath` and `currentPathIndex` as read-only script state.

## Pathfinding behavior

Path endpoints are snapped to the nearest walkable cell. Returned waypoints are world-space points with straight runs merged, but they are not geometrically smoothed.


---

<!-- page: docs/editor/lighting-audio-ui.html -->
# Lighting, audio & UI

> Build atmospheric scenes, sound behavior and responsive UI with Realot Studio components.

> **Exact control path:** Create lights from GameObject → Light or add Light/Audio/UI components through Inspector → Add Component . Screen-space UI entities can also be created directly from the top UI menu.

## Lighting

Lights support Directional, Point, Spot, Area, GodRays and Freeform types. LightingSettings controls scene-wide shadow quality, ambient darkness and visible glow strength. ShadowCaster controls per-entity shadow geometry and softness.

## Shadow quality

ShadowMode `quad` is the cheaper analytic mode. `raymarch` enables per-pixel ray-marched occlusion; `raymarchSteps` controls accuracy/cost and is clamped to 1-200.

## UI

TextRenderer can be screen-space, while SpeechBubble, ChatLog, TextInput and Joystick provide higher-level UI behaviors. TextInput exposes `justSubmitted`; Joystick exposes normalized x/y input and engagement state.

## Audio listeners

AudioSource can be 3D distance-attenuated. AudioListener receives hearing-area transitions that map to `onHearSound(source)` and `onLoseSound(source)`.


---

<!-- page: docs/editor/tilemaps.html -->
# Tilemaps & tilesets

> Author sparse tile grids and 16-role autotile tilesets.

> **Exact control path:** Create a reusable tileset via GameObject → 2D Object → Tileset and the tile grid via GameObject → 2D Object → Tilemap . Once present, T selects tile painting and Y selects erase. The Tileset Editor exposes the 4×4 role grid and import actions.

## Tileset authoring

The editor can take one image and auto-slice it into a 4×4 role grid, or accept up to 16 separate role images. The stored result is sixteen role-to-sprite-key mappings.

## The 16 roles

The canonical order is `cornerTL, edgeT, cornerTR, stubT, edgeL, center, edgeR, lineV, cornerBL, edgeB, cornerBR, stubB, stubL, lineH, stubR, single`.

## Tilemap data

A Tilemap references a Tileset by entity ID and stores a sparse set of filled cells keyed as `col,row`. The runtime computes the visual tile role from orthogonal neighbors; it does not store the final role per cell.

## Scripting

> **No direct Tilemap script module:** Tilemap/Tileset are editor/scene-data components. There is currently no documented this.tilemap runtime API.


---

<!-- page: docs/editor/component-workflows.html -->
# Components: complete workflow

> A complete guide to adding, configuring, testing, removing, and scripting components. This page complements each individual component reference; it does not replace the per-component settings tables.

## 1. Select the entity first

Click an entity in the **Hierarchy** on the left or select it in the Scene viewport. The selected entity's properties appear in the **Inspector** on the right.

## 2. Add a component

At the bottom of the Inspector click **Add Component**. A centered **Add Component** modal opens with a search field and a scrollable list. Type the component name, then click its row. The list excludes components the entity already has.

## 3. Configure the component

After adding it, scroll the Inspector to the new component section. Start with the component's mode/type field if it has one. Changing a mode can expose or hide related settings. Configure required references/assets before tuning numbers.

## 4. Understand values versus runtime state

Serialized authoring settings are saved with the scene. Runtime state fields can change while the game runs and are useful for debugging. Examples include Rigidbody2D velocity/ground state and CharacterController request/state values.

## 5. Test in Play mode

Run the game, observe the result, and inspect the component again when debugging. Change one setting at a time so you can identify which property caused the behavior.

## 6. Use the dedicated editor tools

| System | Where | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sprite | Inspector SpriteRenderer section / asset picker | Assign the visual asset. |
| Animation | SpriteAnimation → Open Animation Window | Create and edit clips/frames. |
| Physics | Collider/Transform gizmos in Scene viewport | Visually inspect/edit geometry. |
| Navigation | NavWorld2D + navigation toolbar + Edit → Nav Areas… | Author areas, bake/debug navigation, then use NavAgent2D. |
| Tiles | Tileset/Tilemap panels | Create tile data and paint the map. |
| Stroke Path | Stroke Path viewport tool/gizmo | Edit path points and inspect serialized path settings. |
| Scripts | Script → Create New Script / Load Script… / Open Script Editor | Create, attach, edit, and enable scripts. |
| Lighting | Light/ShadowCaster gizmos + Inspector | Author light geometry and shadow participation. |

## 7. Component combinations that matter

- **Dynamic physics actor:** Rigidbody2D + Collider2D; add SpriteRenderer/ShapeRenderer for visuals.
- **Platformer controller:** Rigidbody2D + Collider2D + CharacterController; choose Platformer and configure its movement group.
- **Navigation agent:** NavWorld2D in the navigation world + NavAgent2D on the moving entity; bake/configure the world before testing agent movement.
- **Animated character:** SpriteRenderer + SpriteAnimation, optionally with Rigidbody2D/CharacterController.
- **Interactive UI:** the appropriate UI component (TextRenderer, TextInput, Joystick, SpeechBubble, ChatLog) plus Script when behavior is needed.

## 8. Where to go next

Use the component reference for the complete field table, defaults, API members, notes, and examples. Use [Navigation: Complete Setup](../scripting/navigation-complete.html) for multi-system navigation. Use [Script API Cookbook](../scripting/api-cookbook.html) for complete scripting recipes.

<!-- page: docs/editor/complete-feature-workflows.html -->
# Complete feature workflows

> Use these pages when you need to build an entire subsystem, not just understand one property. Each workflow starts with prerequisites and editor locations, then moves through configuration, scripting, testing and troubleshooting.

### [Navigation authoring](../editor/navigation.html)

Create Nav World 2D, configure bounds/cell size, define areas, paint or derive walkable space, add agents, bake/update navigation and debug the result.

### [Navigation from editor to script](../scripting/navigation-complete.html)

Complete path from scene setup through NavAgent2D, named area masks/costs, navMoveToward/navDriveToward and runtime troubleshooting.

### [Physics authoring](../editor/physics.html)

Build colliders, rigidbodies, joints and character controllers, then tune layers, masks, gravity, damping, slopes and one-way platforms.

### [Physics scripting](../scripting/physics.html)

Use Rigidbody2D, Collider2D, raycasts, forces/impulses, collision state and movement APIs from scripts.

### [Lighting, audio and UI](../editor/lighting-audio-ui.html)

Set up lights/shadows, audio sources/listeners, text and interactive UI components with their editor locations and runtime APIs.

### [Tilemaps and tilesets](../editor/tilemaps.html)

Create tileset data, attach it to a Tilemap, paint, edit tile data and understand the navigation/physics consequences of tile geometry.

### [Assets and animation](../editor/assets-animation.html)

Import/use sprites, build Sprite Animation clips, choose frames, set playback and connect animation state to scripts.

### [Prefabs](../editor/prefabs.html)

Create reusable entity templates, instantiate them, understand overrides, update/revert behavior and runtime spawning.

### [Web/PWA deployment](../export/web.html)

Understand the normal online workflow, standalone web export, PWA behavior and what a deployment must serve.

### [Android APK export](../export/android.html)

Configure the separate build-server workflow and understand what is sent from the browser editor.

## How to use these guides

1. Start with the prerequisites section.
2. Follow the exact editor path instead of guessing which panel contains a control.
3. Configure the minimum working setup first.
4. Only then add optional tuning such as costs, smoothing, avoidance, shadows, custom input or advanced physics.
5. Run the smallest test scene before integrating the subsystem into a large project.
6. If a result is wrong, use the troubleshooting section before changing unrelated settings.

<!-- page: docs/scripting/lifecycle.html -->
# Lifecycle

> Complete Realot Studio script lifecycle and callback reference.

## Core lifecycle

| Callback | Semantics |
| --- | --- |
| onStart() | Once before first onUpdate(). |
| onClone() | Once for runtime clones, immediately before onStart(). |
| onUpdate(dt) | Every render frame. |
| onFixedUpdate(dt) | Fixed 60 Hz accumulator. |
| onDestroy() | Before entity removal / scene end. |

```
function onStart() {
  this.hp = 100; // custom fields on this persist across the entity’s lifetime
  debug.log("HP", this.hp);
}

function onUpdate() {
  this.x += 50 * time.deltaTime; // frame-rate independent movement
}

function onFixedUpdate(dt) {
  // runs at a fixed 60 Hz step — good for deterministic physics-adjacent logic
}

function onDestroy() {
  debug.clear("HP");
}
```

## Pointer callbacks

`onClick()` is a frame pulse for mouse/finger presses targeting an entity with Collider2D. For continuous polling, use `this.isPointerOver`, `this.isClicked`, `this.isTouchOver` or `this.isTapped` where appropriate.

```
function onClick() {
  this.destroy(); // pops this entity when clicked or tapped
}
```

## Collision callbacks

| Callback | Runs |
| --- | --- |
| onCollision(other) | Alias of collision-enter behavior. |
| onCollisionEnter(other) | Contact begins. |
| onCollisionStay(other) | Every physics step while still touching. |
| onCollisionExit(other) | Contact ends. |
| onTriggerEnter(other) | Trigger overlap begins. |
| onTriggerExit(other) | Trigger overlap ends. |

```
function onCollisionEnter(other) {
  if (other.name === "Ground") this.isGrounded = true;
}

function onTriggerEnter(other) {
  if (other.hasComponent("Rigidbody2D")) scene.load("Level2");
}
```

## State callbacks

When using `this.state.change(name)`, Realot Studio can call `onStateExit()`, `onStateEnter()` and `onStateUpdate(dt)` for state-specific logic.

```
function onUpdate() {
  if (this.hp <= 0 && this.state.current !== "dead") {
    this.state.change("dead");
  }
}

function onStateEnter() {
  if (this.state.current === "dead") this.sprite.opacity = 0.3;
}
```

## Error isolation

Lifecycle errors are caught and reported by the runtime. A one-time `onStart()` failure disables the script; recurring `onUpdate()` errors are isolated so the next frame can continue.


---

<!-- page: docs/scripting/globals.html -->
# Global scripting API

> Reference for every built-in global function and service object available inside Realot Studio scripts.

## Entity lookup

| Function | Returns / behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `findFirst(name)` | First entity with this name, or `null`. |
| `findAll(name)` | All entities with this name. |
| `findFirstWithTag(tag)` | First entity with this tag, or `null`. |
| `findAllWithTag(tag)` | All entities with this tag. |
| `findWithTag(tag)` | Alias for `findAllWithTag(tag)`. |
| `findById(id)` | Entity with this exact stable ID, or `null`. |
| `findInRadius(x, y, radius, opts?)` | Nearby entities, nearest first. Optional filters can narrow the search. |

## Scene (`scene`)

`scene` contains the same entity-lookup functions above, plus `load(sceneName)`, `restart()`, `pause()`, `resume()`, the read-only properties `current` and `isPaused`, and scene-wide `lighting`. `scene.pause()` freezes gameplay simulation while leaving the editor/Play window responsive; call `scene.resume()` to continue.

## Physics (`physics`)

`physics.raycast(x1, y1, x2, y2, opts?)` casts a ray against Rapier collider shapes and returns the closest hit or `null`. A hit contains the entity, world point, surface normal (when available) and distance. Pass `{ exclude: [this] }` to skip an entity, `{ debug: true }` to draw the ray for one frame, or `{ layerMask: physics.layer(0, 2) }` to filter by layer bits. `physics.layer(...indices)` creates the bitmask for slots 0–15.

```
function onUpdate() {
  var hit = physics.raycast(this.x, this.y, this.x + 200, this.y, {
    exclude: [this],
    debug: true
  });
  if (hit) debug.log("Ray hit", hit.entity.name);
}
```

## Navigation (`nav`)

| Member | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `findPath(x1, y1, x2, y2, opts?)` | Returns world-space waypoints or `null` when no route is available. |
| `isWalkable(x, y)` | Tests whether a world point falls on a walkable navigation cell. |
| `bake()` | Rebuilds the scene NavWorld2D from current colliders; returns walkable/blocked counts or `null`. |
| `areaIndex(name)` | Resolves an area name to a slot index, or `-1`. |
| `areaMask(...names)` | Builds a bitmask from named areas. |
| `areaCosts(costsByName)` | Builds a 16-entry cost array from area names and positive costs. |

For moving entities every frame, use `this.navMoveToward()` or (for a Car controller) `this.navDriveToward()`. See [Pathfinding](navigation.html).

## Keyboard (`input`)

`input.keyDown(key)` is true while a key is held. `input.keyPressed(key)` is true only on the frame it is first pressed. Both accept `"Any"` to test whether any key is held or was pressed that frame. Use the [Input guide](input.html) for key naming and patterns.

## Mouse and pointer (`mouse`)

`mouse.x` and `mouse.y` are world coordinates. `screenX` and `screenY` are canvas pixels. `over` reports whether the pointer is over the game canvas. `down(button?)`, `pressed(button?)` and `released(button?)` read mouse buttons (0 left, 1 middle, 2 right; omitted means left). `isOver(entityOrName, opts?)` tests hover and `clickedOn(entityOrName, opts?, button?)` tests a click on a specific entity.

## Touch (`touch`)

`touch` is a live array of active touches. Each touch exposes `id`, world-space `x/y`, canvas-pixel `screenX/screenY`, start coordinates, displacement (`dx/dy`), `distance`, and one-frame `justStarted/justEnded` flags. The array also exposes `count`, `first`, `anyJustStarted` and `anyJustEnded`. Gesture helpers are `swipe.active/direction/dx/dy/distance` and `pinch.active/scale/delta/distance`. `touch.isOver(entityOrName, opts?)` checks a finger over an entity; `touch.tappedOn(entityOrName, opts?)` detects the initial tap. See [Input guide](input.html).

## Time (`time`)

`time.deltaTime` is scaled frame time, `time.unscaledDeltaTime` is frame time before time scaling, `time.elapsed` is elapsed game time, and `time.scale` controls game speed. A scale of 0 pauses time-driven simulation; 1 is normal speed. See [Time scale & game speed](time-scale.html).

## Random and math helpers

`random.int(min, max)` returns an inclusive random integer. `random.float(min, max)` returns a random float in the half-open range [min, max). `mathx` provides `lerp`, `smoothstep`, `clamp`, `moveToward`, `remap` and `approximately`. A bare `smoothstep(a, b, value)` global is also available. Native JavaScript `Math` is available as well.

## Shared in-memory state (`global`)

`global` is a shared key/value object visible to all scripts in the current running game. Read and write named properties directly, for example `global.score = 10`. It is memory-only; it does not survive reloading the game page. Use `save` for persistent data.

## Persistent save data (`save`)

`save` stores JSON-safe values in IndexedDB, separated into named save slots. Its full 13-member API is listed in [SaveAPI](../api/script-modules.html#saveapi). Common calls are `get`, `set`, `has`, `delete`, `keys` and `clear`. Use `await save.load("slot2")` to change slots, `await save.listSlots()` to list them, `await save.deleteSlot("slot2")` to remove a slot, and `await save.flushNow()` to wait for pending writes. See [Persistence](persistence.html).

## Debug HUD (`debug`)

`debug.show()` enables the gameplay HUD and system timing display in the Play window; `debug.show(false)` turns it off. `debug.showFps(false)` hides only its FPS line. `debug.log(label, value)` adds or updates a custom line; `debug.clear(label)` removes one line; `debug.clearAll()` removes all custom lines. This is separate from the editor Console.

## Object pools (`pool`)

`pool.create(name, options)` creates a named pool using a source prefab, scene entity or EntityContext. `pool.find(name)` retrieves a named pool, `pool.get(name, x, y)` gets an active object, and `pool.release(entity)` returns it for reuse. A pooled entity can call `this.releaseToPool(delay?)`. Pooled scripts can use `onEnable` and `onDisable` for work that should run each time an object is borrowed or returned.

## Spawn, timers, messages and tweens

| Function | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `spawn(nameOrTag, opts?)` | Clones an entity found by name, or by tag when `opts.byTag` is true. Returns an EntityContext or `null`. |
| `wait(seconds, callback)` | Runs once after game time passes; returns a timer ID. |
| `repeat(seconds, callback)` | Runs repeatedly at the interval; returns a timer ID. |
| `cancelWait(id)` / `cancelRepeat(id)` | Cancel the matching timer. Entity-owned timers also stop when their owner is destroyed or the scene changes. |
| `sendMessage(tagOrEntity, message, data?)` | Sends to all scripts matching a tag, or one exact entity context. |
| `broadcastMessage(message, data?)` | Sends to every script in the current scene. |
| `tween(target, properties, duration, easing?, onComplete?)` | Animates numeric properties over game time; returns an ID. |
| `cancelTween(id)` | Cancels a running tween. |

Read [Timers, state & messaging](timers-state.html), [Finding and spawning](finding-entities.html) and [Tween API](tween.html) for complete examples and option details. The [script module index](../api/script-modules.html) contains all 24 component/global API module allow-lists.


---

<!-- page: docs/scripting/tween.html -->
# Tween API

> Animate numeric properties smoothly with tween(), choose from 33 easing curves, and stop animations with cancelTween().

## Overview

`tween(target, properties, duration, easing, onComplete)` smoothly moves one or more numeric properties from their current value to a target value over a number of **game seconds**. It is a global function, available in every script with no import. It returns a numeric id you can pass to `cancelTween(id)`.

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | object | An entity context (`this`, or the result of `findFirst()` etc.) or a scripting component object such as `this.sprite`, `this.light` or `this.camera`. |
| `properties` | object | Map of property name to end value, for example `{ x: 420, y: 180 }`. Only finite numbers are accepted as end values. |
| `duration` | number | Length in game seconds. `0` (or an invalid value) completes on the next tween update. |
| `easing` | string | Optional. One of the [33 easing names](#easing-catalogue). Empty or omitted means `"linear"`. |
| `onComplete` | function | Optional. Called once when the tween finishes, with `this` bound to the entity that started the tween. |

```
function onStart() {
  // Move, spin and resize over 0.8 game seconds
  tween(this, { x: 420, y: 180, rotation: 90, scaleX: 1.2, scaleY: 1.2 }, 0.8, "easeOutCubic", function () {
    // "this" is still the entity that started the tween
    tween(this.sprite, { opacity: 0.25 }, 0.35, "easeInOutSine");
  });
}
```

## What can be tweened

A property is tweened only if it **already exists on the target and currently holds a finite number**. Properties that are missing, non-numeric (colours are hex strings, `position` and `scale` are objects) or non-finite are skipped.

| Target | Typical tweenable properties |
| --- | --- |
| `this` (entity) | `x`, `y`, `rotation`, `scaleX`, `scaleY` |
| `this.sprite` | `opacity` |
| `this.shape` | `width`, `height`, `radius`, `opacity`, `outlineWidth` |
| `this.text` | `fontSize`, `opacity` |
| `this.light` | `intensity`, `radius`, `angle`, `shadowStrength` |
| `this.audio` | `volume`, `pitch` |
| `this.camera` | `zoom`, `offsetX`, `offsetY` |
| `this.strokePath` | `thickness`, `opacity`, `textureOffset` |
| `scene.lighting` | `ambientDarkness`, `glowStrength` |

Any numeric member listed on a component's Script API table can be a tween target. Each tween writes through the normal script API, so setter rules (clamping, validation) still apply.

## Cancelling

```
var id = tween(this, { x: 700 }, 2, "easeOutBounce");
// later
var wasActive = cancelTween(id);   // true only if a tween with that id was still running
```

`cancelTween()` leaves the property at whatever value it had reached. `onComplete` is not called for a cancelled tween.

## Behavior and rules

- **Start tweens from lifecycle callbacks** such as `onStart()`, `onClick()` or a collision handler. Calling `tween()` outside script execution logs `[tween]` warning and returns `-1`. Avoid creating a new tween every frame in `onUpdate()`; start one and let it run.
- **Game time.** Tweens advance once per frame after `onUpdate` callbacks, using the scaled frame clock. [`time.scale`](time-scale.html) speeds them up or slows them down, and `scene.pause()` freezes them.
- **Exact finish.** When progress reaches 1 the property is set to the exact end value, so back/elastic overshoot never leaves a rounding error.
- **Several properties at once** in one call share the same duration and easing.
- **Automatic cleanup.** A tween ends silently if the entity that started it, or the entity it targets, is destroyed. Restarting or switching scenes clears all tweens.
- **Errors.** If an easing function or a property setter throws, that tween is removed and the error is reported in the Console with the owning entity name. A completion callback that throws is reported as `tween onComplete`.
- **Return value.** Invalid input (bad target, properties not an object, unknown easing, no numeric properties, non-function `onComplete`) returns `-1` and logs a `[tween]` warning that says what to fix. An unknown easing name is never silently treated as linear.
- **Easing names** are case-insensitive and ignore spaces, hyphens and underscores, so `"EASE-OUT-QUAD"` equals `"easeOutQuad"`.

> **Tweening physics bodies:** Assigning x or y on an entity that has a Dynamic or Kinematic Rigidbody2D teleports the body each frame. For moving physics objects use velocities or forces; use tween for transforms, opacity, UI, lights, cameras and Static or non-physics entities.

## Editor support

The Script Editor autocompletes `tween` and `cancelTween`, and offers the easing names inside the easing string (type `tween(this, { x: 100 }, 1, "easeOut` and the matching names appear). Both names are syntax-highlighted as engine globals.

## Easing catalogue

Every name below is a real engine easing. Each preview is drawn from the engine's own easing function: the horizontal axis is time (0 to 1) and the vertical axis is progress. The dashed lines mark the start value (bottom) and end value (top); curves that cross them overshoot on purpose. **In** starts slowly, **Out** ends slowly, **InOut** does both.

| Family | Names |
| --- | --- |
| Basic | `linear`, `smoothstep`, `smootherstep` |
| Quad | `easeInQuad`, `easeOutQuad`, `easeInOutQuad` |
| Cubic | `easeInCubic`, `easeOutCubic`, `easeInOutCubic` |
| Quart | `easeInQuart`, `easeOutQuart`, `easeInOutQuart` |
| Quint | `easeInQuint`, `easeOutQuint`, `easeInOutQuint` |
| Sine | `easeInSine`, `easeOutSine`, `easeInOutSine` |
| Expo | `easeInExpo`, `easeOutExpo`, `easeInOutExpo` |
| Circ | `easeInCirc`, `easeOutCirc`, `easeInOutCirc` |
| Back | `easeInBack`, `easeOutBack`, `easeInOutBack` |
| Elastic | `easeInElastic`, `easeOutElastic`, `easeInOutElastic` |
| Bounce | `easeInBounce`, `easeOutBounce`, `easeInOutBounce` |
