<!-- page: docs/export/index.html -->
# Export overview

> Choose a standalone web export or the built-in Android APK build workflow.

## Available export targets

| Target | Availability | What it creates |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTML5 | Available | A standalone static game package with `index.html` and the required runtime/assets. |
| PWA | Available | The HTML5 game package plus a web manifest and service worker for installable/offline behavior. |
| Android APK | Available through the configured build service | A debug-signed APK generated remotely from the same standalone web package. |
| Desktop (Windows/Mac/Linux) | Coming soon / disabled | Not currently generated by the Export window. |

Open **File → Export…** or the toolbar's **Export** button. See [Export window reference](export-window.html) for the controls and [Android APK](android.html) for the service workflow.

## Standalone game package

The browser builds a standalone ZIP with `index.html` at its root, a game entry script, runtime files and referenced assets. It does not include the editor or Hub. The Android build flow consumes this same standalone export package rather than reconstructing a game from editor-only project data.

## Run a web export

Serve the exported folder through HTTP(S) or upload it to a static host. Do not double-click `index.html` from the file system: browser module and asset requests can fail under `file://`.


---

<!-- page: docs/export/web.html -->
# HTML5 and PWA export

> Create a standalone HTML5 game or a PWA with a manifest and service worker.

## HTML5

HTML5 export produces a standalone static game package. The ZIP contains an `index.html` entry point, game code, the standalone runtime and the assets required by the project. It does not include the editor or Hub.

## PWA

PWA export adds a web app manifest and service worker to the same standalone game package. The browser can offer installation and offline caching when the deployment meets the browser's PWA requirements.

## Hosting checklist

- Extract the ZIP and keep the entry point, runtime and referenced assets together.
- Serve the package over HTTP(S); do not rely on opening `index.html` directly with `file://`.
- Use HTTPS on a public deployment when browser security rules or PWA installation require a secure origin.
- Test the exported game independently of the editor before sharing it.


---

<!-- page: docs/export/export-window.html -->
# Export window reference

> Understand the game title, favicon, export formats, build progress and Android APK quota.

Open the Export window from **File → Export…** or the toolbar's **Export** button.

## Game details

| Field | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Game title | Up to 80 characters; defaults to the project name. Used for the exported page title and Android app name. |
| Favicon | Optional image selected in the Export window. It is used as the exported web game's icon and, where supported by the APK wrapper, the Android launcher icon. |

## Format cards

| Card | Status | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTML5 | Available | Standalone static game package. |
| PWA | Available | HTML5 package plus manifest and service worker. |
| Desktop (Windows/Mac/Linux) | Coming soon / disabled | Not generated by the current Export window. |
| Android APK | Available | A debug-signed APK built by the configured remote service. |

## Browser-side web packaging

- HTML5/PWA packaging runs in the browser.
- The exporter includes the game runtime and referenced assets, not the editor.
- When asset optimization is supported by the browser, images/audio may be re-encoded and checked before inclusion.
- The result is a downloadable ZIP. Use a local HTTP server or static host to run it; direct `file://` opening is not supported.

## Android APK workflow

The Android card uses the built-in service configured for this Realot deployment. The editor prepares the standalone game ZIP, requests or renews a temporary build token, uploads the ZIP, polls the job and downloads the APK. You do not add a custom build server or paste an API key into the Export window.

The card shows the service connection state and the remaining APK export allowance. The current client-side allowance is **3 accepted builds in a rolling 14-day window per browser**; the authoritative service may apply additional server-side limits.

## Progress and cancellation

While an APK is building, the Export window displays progress and offers **Cancel build**. The editor polls the job approximately every 2.5 seconds and uses a 10-minute client timeout. Cancelling or leaving the editor signals cancellation to the service when possible. HTML5 and PWA packaging occurs locally in the browser.

## Build an APK from a web export

After an HTML5 or PWA export, the result screen can offer **Build APK from this HTML5/PWA export**. This sends the exact web ZIP already created, so the game package does not need to be rebuilt.


---

<!-- page: docs/export/android.html -->
# Export an Android APK

> Build an Android APK directly from the Realot Studio Export window. The current editor allows three APK exports in a rolling 14-day period.

> **One simple flow:** Click Export , choose Android APK , and let Realot build the file. There is no separate setup wizard or need to export HTML5 first.

## Steps

1. Open the game project in Realot Studio.
2. Click **Export** in the editor toolbar. You can also use **File → Export…**.
3. In the Export Game window, choose **Android APK**.
4. Wait for the build to finish. Realot downloads the finished `.apk` file to your device.

The game title is filled in from the project name and can be changed before exporting. Choosing a custom favicon is optional. Those are the only optional details shown in the export form; you do not need Android Studio, Gradle, the Android SDK or a separate web export.

## APK export limit

The current editor allows **3 APK exports in a rolling 14-day period**. The Export window shows how many of the three remain and explains when an export becomes available again. The window is rolling: an export becomes available again 14 days after the corresponding counted export, rather than all three resetting on one calendar date.

An export is counted after the build service accepts the job. A failed or cancelled build gives that export back. **HTML5 and PWA exports are not limited by the APK quota.**

> **Quota detail for support and AI tools:** The supplied browser client records the rolling quota in this browser's local storage. It is therefore a per-browser client allowance, not an account-based counter. The build service should enforce its own server-side usage limits; clearing browser data is not a supported way to manage exports.

## What the APK contains

The current Android option produces a **debug-signed APK** intended for testing and direct installation on an Android device. It is not a Play Store production-signed release. The Android build service is needed to create the APK; the downloaded game does not need to contact that service while it is running.

## When an export does not finish

Read the message shown in the Export window. If the service is waking up or temporarily unavailable, try again later. A failed or cancelled build returns the consumed export allowance. If the same error keeps happening, copy the message from the export window and include it when reporting the issue.

## Other export formats

- **HTML5:** creates a standalone web game you can host as a static site.
- **PWA:** creates the web game plus an installable manifest and service worker for offline use.
- **Desktop (Windows/Mac/Linux):** listed in the format picker as coming soon in the supplied engine build.

For the other formats, see [HTML5 and PWA export](web.html) or the [Export window reference](export-window.html).


---

<!-- page: docs/reference/tuning-guide.html -->
# Tuning guide

> Practical “increase/decrease this” rules for movement, physics, navigation, lighting, UI and path authoring.

## How to tune movement

| Goal | Raise | Lower |
| --- | --- | --- |
| More responsive character movement | acceleration, airControl | acceleration, airControl |
| Longer/faster jump | jumpForce, maxJumps if desired | gravityScale / jumpForce |
| More stable vehicle | turn/brake smoothing, recovery settings | overly aggressive steering values |
| Faster NavAgent | speed, acceleration | stoppingDistance if you want it closer before stopping |

## How to tune physics

| Goal | Typical setting | Direction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Make dynamic body fall faster | Rigidbody2D.gravityScale | Increase above 1. |
| Make body coast longer | linearDamping | Decrease toward 0. |
| Make body stop rotating sooner | angularDamping | Increase. |
| Make contact bouncier | Collider2D.restitution | Increase. |
| Reduce sliding | Collider2D.friction | Increase. |
| Make a platform one-way | Collider2D.isOneWayPlatform | Enable; contact filtering then only allows landing from the supported side. |

## How to tune navigation

| Setting | Increase means | Decrease means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NavWorld2D.cellSize | coarser/faster grid, less geometric detail | finer grid, narrower detail but more work |
| NavAgent2D.radius | larger clearance requirement | smaller agent clearance |
| NavAgent2D.repathInterval | less frequent replanning | more responsive replanning |
| NavWorld2D.areaCosts slot | more expensive path cost through that area | closer to the cheapest route |

## How to tune lighting

| Setting | Increase means | Decrease means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Light.intensity | brighter/stronger contribution | dimmer |
| Light.radius | larger influence region | tighter/localized light |
| ShadowCaster.length | longer shadow reach | shorter/contact shadow |
| ShadowCaster.softness | softer/wider penumbra | crisper edge |
| LightingSettings.raymarchSteps | more samples/detail, more GPU work | less GPU work, potentially less detail |
| LightingSettings.ambientDarkness | darker unlit regions | brighter ambient base |

> **Rule for numeric documentation:** Realot Studio documentation should state not only what a field is, but what increasing and decreasing it does, its units, default, and whether the value is clamped/validated. The API catalog in api-options.json follows this model for option objects.


---

<!-- page: docs/reference/scene-format.html -->
# Scene JSON

> Reference the Realot Studio scene serialization format.

## Top-level shape

```
{
  "sceneName": "Level1",
  "hierarchyFolders": [],
  "entities": []
}
```

## Entity shape

```
{
  "id": "e12",
  "name": "Target",
  "tag": "Target",
  "active": true,
  "folderId": null,
  "prefabId": null,
  "prefabOverrides": {},
  "components": {
    "Transform": { "x": 0, "y": 0, "z": 0, "rotation": 0, "scaleX": 1, "scaleY": 1 }
  }
}
```

## Component registry

SceneSerializer recognizes the runtime component types: Transform, Camera, SpriteRenderer, ShapeRenderer, StrokePath, TextRenderer, SpeechBubble, ChatLog, TextInput, Joystick, Rigidbody2D, Collider2D, Joint2D, Light, ShadowCaster, CharacterController, LightingSettings, SpriteAnimation, AudioSource, AudioListener, Tileset, Tilemap, NavWorld2D, NavAgent2D and Script.

## Authoring rules

Scene files are plain JSON and can be authored by the editor, generated by tools or hand-written. The serializer deep-copies folder/prefab override data so saved snapshots do not alias live state.

## Default camera

A fresh/default scene uses a **Main Camera** entity with tag `MainCamera`, active state enabled, Transform at 0,0 and a main Camera flag.


---

<!-- page: docs/reference/project-format.html -->
# Project format

> Understand the portable .realot archive and the difference between editable projects and standalone game exports.

## Current project file

**Save Project** downloads a `.realot` file. The extension identifies Realot's portable project file, which the editor reads as a complete project package.

## Archive contents

| Entry | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `manifest.json` | Project name, engine compatibility metadata and save information. |
| `scenes/index.json` | Scene list and active scene information. |
| `scenes/*.json` | Serialized scene entities and component data. |
| `assets/sprites.json`, `frames.json`, `audio.json` | Asset catalogues and references to binary asset files. |
| `assets/bin/` | Binary image/audio data referenced by the asset catalogues. |
| `scripts.json` | User-authored JavaScript source. |
| `prefabs.json` | Saved prefab definitions. |
| `layers.json`, `navAreas.json`, `tags.json` | Project-wide layer, navigation-area and tag names. |

## Open a project

Use the editor's **File → Load Project** command to open a saved `.realot` project. On a desktop browser that supports PWA file handling, you can also install Realot Hub and double-click a downloaded `.realot` file to open it in the editor.

## Project archive versus game export

A `.realot` archive is an editable project that can be loaded back into the editor. An HTML5/PWA export is a separate standalone game package with `index.html` at its root, containing the runtime and files needed to run the game. The Android build service consumes the standalone game export, not the editable project file.

## Compatibility metadata

The project manifest includes engine compatibility metadata. The loader compares it with the engine build and can warn when a project was saved by a newer engine. This metadata belongs to the project format; it is not a documentation version or a user-facing engine download version.


---

<!-- page: docs/reference/rules.html -->
# Engine conventions (RULES.txt)

> The architectural rules that govern how Realot Studio’s own codebase is organized.

## Scope

This is the engine’s own internal contract for where code goes and how the three top-level folders relate. It applies to people extending Realot Studio itself; if you’re only writing game scripts, you don’t need it — see Scripting quickstart instead.

## 1. The core rule: runtime never depends on editor

`runtime/` is the actual game engine. `editor/` is the Unity-style level editor UI, a development tool only. `target/` is the standalone game shell, importing only from `runtime/`. No file under `runtime/` may ever import, reference, or depend on anything under `editor/` — not for debugging, not temporarily, not ever. You must be able to delete the `editor/` folder entirely and the game (`standalone runtime play entry point`) keeps working with zero changes. `editor/` may import from `runtime/` — that direction is allowed and expected, since the editor is built on top of the engine.

## 2. One feature = new file(s), not a growing old file

Adding a new component, system, editor panel, scripting API, or asset type creates a new file in the appropriate subfolder. Unrelated functionality is never appended into an existing file just because it’s nearby or already open. If a feature doesn’t fit any existing subfolder, a new subfolder is created (matching the existing lowercase, pluralized naming style) rather than dumping it into an unrelated folder.

| Adding… | Goes in… |
| --- | --- |
| A new gameplay component | runtime/components/YourComponent.js |
| A new gameplay/rendering/physics system | runtime/systems/YourSystem.js |
| A new editor panel | editor/panels/YourPanel.js |
| A new asset type | runtime/assets/YourManager.js |
| A new scripting capability | A method/property on the relevant file in runtime/scripting/components/, or a new file there |

## 3. Components stay plain data

Files under `runtime/components/` hold only plain serializable data (numbers, strings, booleans). No PixiJS objects, no DOM references, no behavior/update logic — behavior belongs in `runtime/systems/`. This is what keeps SceneSerializer.js able to save and load any component generically.

## 4. Rendering is centralized

`runtime/systems/RenderSystem.js` is the only place that creates or updates PixiJS display objects from entity data. Both the editor’s viewport and the standalone target use it, so visuals never drift between edit mode and play mode. Editor-only chrome (grid lines, selection gizmos) may be drawn in its own separate layer on top of the runtime’s render output — that chrome must never be visible in `/target`.

## 5. Scene data flows through the runtime’s public API only

The editor never invents its own scene format or its own copy of scene state. The single source of truth is the live World instance, and the single way to read/write its persisted form is `runtime/scene/SceneSerializer.js`. New scene-level functionality (undo, multi-scene, prefabs) extends the runtime’s `scene/` folder, not the editor’s `state/` folder.

## One API per capability (scripting)

`this.x`, `this.y`, `this.position`, `this.rotation`, `this.translate()`, and `this.visible` are flat shortcuts because Transform has only one shape. Everything else — velocity, physics forces, sprite properties, animation, camera, audio, movement-type tunables — is reached only through its sub-object (`this.rigidbody.*`, `this.sprite.*`, `this.controller.*`, etc). There is deliberately no flat-shortcut duplicate of any of these, because RigidbodyAPI exposes a different shape per body type and ControllerAPI exposes a different shape per controller type — a second flat copy would either duplicate that per-type logic or drift out of sync with it.

> **Source note:** These rules come from the engine repository’s RULES.txt . That file is not included in the client distribution ( project/ contains editor/ , player/ , runtime/ and vendor/ only), so it is documented here rather than linked.


---

<!-- page: docs/reference/debugging.html -->
# Debugging

> Diagnose common Realot Studio runtime and authoring problems.

## Use the Debug HUD

The `debug` module can show the HUD, FPS and logging. Performance/profiling displays are useful while diagnosing update and rendering behavior.

## Lifecycle failures

If a lifecycle callback throws, the runtime reports the error and isolates it. Look for the callback name and error classification in the runtime output.

## Physics checklist

- Confirm the entity has the expected Rigidbody2D body type.
- Confirm Collider2D shape, layer and mask settings.
- For one-way platforms, test motion from both sides.
- Use `physics.raycast(...,{debug:true})` to verify what the query actually sees.

## Navigation checklist

- Confirm a NavWorld2D exists in the scene.
- Confirm the queried point is inside walkable bounds.
- Check NavAgent2D radius/area settings.
- Use `nav.findPath(...,{debug:true})` to visualize the result.

## Common API mistake

> **Editor code is not game code:** If code is only found in project/editor/ , it is not automatically a supported game-script API. The public script surface is the documented this.\* context and global runtime modules.


---

<!-- page: docs/reference/security.html -->
# Security and play origin

> Understand the script trust boundary and why shared projects should run on a separate origin.

> **Game scripts are not a security sandbox:** Project scripts execute as ordinary JavaScript in the game page. Treat scripts inside imported projects as code from another person, not as inert project data.

## Script execution

Realot shadows selected browser globals inside its script environment as a guardrail against accidental access. This is not a hardened security boundary: scripts are compiled and run as page code. Do not open a project containing scripts unless you trust its source.

## Use a separate play origin for shared projects

For a deployment where people can open projects from others, configure the editor to launch Play on a separate hostname that serves the same Realot files. In `project/editor/index.html`, set the `realot-play-origin` meta tag to that HTTPS origin:

```
<meta name="realot-play-origin" content="https://play.example.com" />
```

The editor sends the scene to the play page using `postMessage`. Because the two hostnames are different origins, browser same-origin policy keeps the play page's localStorage, IndexedDB and DOM separate from the editor's. Leave the meta content empty and Play uses the same origin; that is less isolated and is not recommended for untrusted projects.

## Offline behavior

If the configured play origin cannot be reached, such as while offline, the editor can fall back to same-origin Play and logs a warning. Data saved by the game on the play origin is separate from the editor origin's storage.

## Other protections

- Messages are accepted only from the corresponding editor/play window and expected origin.
- Console output and project-controlled names are escaped before display in the editor UI.
- Loading a project containing scripts asks for confirmation first.
- Exported games run on the origin where the developer hosts them; they are separate from the editor's Play-origin setting.

## APK build credentials

The APK service URL is public configuration. Permanent service credentials must not be placed in the static editor source because all shipped JavaScript can be inspected by visitors. The editor's intended managed flow requests a short-lived token from the service and renews it when needed. The service must still enforce appropriate quotas and access controls; a public token-issuance endpoint alone does not identify an approved user.


---

<!-- page: docs/reference/live-updates.html -->
# Live updates

> How the hosted Realot Studio website and its documentation are updated in place.

## Browser delivery

Realot Studio is delivered as a web application. The hosted Hub, editor and runtime are loaded from the site's published files. Users do not need to download a new engine installer whenever the site owner publishes an update.

## The website address stays the same

Publishing a new engine build replaces the files served at the existing deployment URL. The same is true of the documentation: its unversioned topic URLs point to the current published documentation.

## Browser and PWA caching

A normal browser visit retrieves the published site files according to the deployment's cache headers. An installed PWA or a browser with the service worker may continue using cached files while offline. Reconnect and reload to allow the new published files to be fetched. A deployment should publish its files atomically and configure cache headers so the HTML entry points and service worker can update.

## Project compatibility is separate

Although the hosted engine is updated in place, saved project archives may contain engine compatibility metadata. When a project saved by a newer engine is opened in an older build, Realot may show a compatibility warning. That project metadata is not a documentation URL version.


---

<!-- page: docs/reference/source-map.html -->
# Source map & verification

> A source-grounded map of where Realot Studio’s public behavior and editor controls are actually implemented.

> **Verified source:** This documentation pass was checked against the supplied Realot Studio engine source, including runtime components, scripting API modules, editor panels/state, navigation, physics, scene serialization, and export code.

## Engine architecture map

| Area | Primary source locations | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Public runtime entry | `project/runtime/index.js` | Wires World + systems + scripting and exposes createGame(). |
| Components | `project/runtime/components/` | Serializable component data used by scene entities. |
| Systems | `project/runtime/systems/` | Runtime behavior such as physics, rendering, animation, lighting, audio, navigation and scripting. |
| Scripting | `project/runtime/scripting/` | User-facing script surface, EntityContext and option metadata. |
| Physics | `project/runtime/physics/` | Rapier-backed collider/body/joint queries and contact behavior. |
| Navigation | `project/runtime/pathfinding/` | A\* grid bake, dynamic bake, area masks/costs and navigation support. |
| Editor UI | `project/editor/panels/` | Toolbar, Hierarchy, Inspector, Project/Console, animation, tileset, export and settings windows. |
| Editor state/events | `project/editor/state/` | Persistence, dirty state, layer/area registries and DOM event handling. |
| Scene serialization | `project/runtime/scene/SceneSerializer.js` | Serialized scene/entity component format. |

## Important source files for documentation truth

| Question | Verify here |
| --- | --- |
| What components exist? | `project/runtime/components/*.js` |
| What script members exist? | `project/runtime/scripting/components/*API.js` + `ScriptAPI.js` |
| What opts are accepted? | `project/runtime/scripting/NavAPI.js` and the relevant ScriptAPI doc comments |
| Where is a button? | `project/editor/panels/*.js` |
| What appears only conditionally? | `project/editor/panels/Toolbar.js` + `editor/state/EditorEvents.js` |
| How does an interaction actually behave? | Relevant runtime system + component + tests in the same area. |

<!-- page: docs/reference/ai-bridge.html -->
# AI Bridge: connect an AI assistant

> Connect an MCP-compatible AI app to the open Realot Studio editor using the built-in shared relay, with optional self-hosting, read-only mode and a complete source-derived tool catalog.

> **Built in and ready to use:** Realot Studio includes a shared relay address. Most users do not need to install Node.js, configure a local server, create a Cloudflare account or deploy anything. Open AI Bridge, copy the private link into an AI app that supports remote MCP connectors, and press Connect in Realot.

## Connect your AI assistant

1. Open your project in Realot Studio and click **AI Bridge** in the editor.
2. Click **Copy link** in the panel.
3. In your AI app, open its connector or MCP-server settings. Add a **remote MCP server** or **custom connector**, paste the copied link, and name it **Realot**. The exact menu name depends on the AI app.
4. Return to Realot and click **Connect**. The panel should show **Connected**. Ask the AI to inspect the open project before asking it to make changes.

The copied link contains a private secret key. Treat it like a password: anyone who has the link may be able to use the tools exposed by your open editor. Do not post it in public messages or commit it to a project repository.

## AI Bridge panel options

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Copy link** | Copies the private remote MCP connector URL for this editor. |
| **Connect / Disconnect** | Starts or closes the editor's connection to the relay. The editor must remain open while the AI works on the live project. |
| **Read-only** | Blocks tools that change the project. The AI can inspect the editor but cannot perform supported edit operations while this is enabled. |
| **Connect automatically when the editor opens** | Remembers the preference and reconnects on a later editor launch when a private key is already configured. |
| **Make a new private link** | Creates a new secret key and invalidates the old link. Add the new link to your AI app; the old connector URL will no longer authenticate. |
| **Need more AI time? → click here to host it** | Opens Cloudflare's deployment flow for an optional personal copy of the relay. This is not needed for the built-in shared relay. |
| **Use it / Default** | *Use it* switches to the relay URL you supplied and refreshes the connector link. *Default* switches back to Realot's built-in shared relay. Re-copy the connector link after changing relay addresses. |

## Shared relay time allowance

The built-in shared relay includes **30 minutes of active AI work in each 24-hour usage window**. Time is counted while a tool call is running and for up to 20 seconds between calls. Being connected while the AI is idle does not use the allowance. The panel shows the remaining time and the reset countdown.

The usage record is kept in this browser's local storage. It is a client-side allowance display and should not be treated as an account-wide quota or a tamper-proof billing record. Hosting your own relay removes the shared-relay active-time limit; Cloudflare account usage and service terms may still apply.

## Optional: host a personal relay

Most users should stay on the built-in relay. Hosting your own is an advanced option for users who want to avoid the shared-relay time allowance or operate their own relay endpoint.

1. In the AI Bridge panel, select **click here to host it**. Realot opens the Cloudflare deployment page for the relay source repository.
2. Complete Cloudflare's deployment and copy the HTTPS address ending in `.workers.dev`.
3. Paste that address into the relay field in the AI Bridge panel and click **Use it**.
4. Click **Copy link** again and replace the old Realot connector URL in your AI app. Connect from the editor.

To return to the shared relay, click **Default**, copy the refreshed link, and update the connector in your AI app. A personal relay has no Realot active-AI-minutes cap, but you are responsible for its deployment, availability and Cloudflare account.

## What the AI can do

The built-in relay currently exposes **80 MCP tools**. They allow an AI app to inspect editor state, scenes and entities; create and modify entities and components; read, write and attach scripts; start or pause play mode; inspect the Console and capture a screenshot; manage assets and chunked uploads; edit animation clips and frames; manage tilesets and tilemaps; paint navigation cells and configure navigation and physics layers; manage tags, folders, prefabs and scenes; save or export project data; and control editor panels and tools.

The tables below list every hosted tool name and its input fields. Fields shown in bold are required. Full JSON input schemas—including exact types, constraints and additional properties—are published in the [machine-readable API catalog](../../api/index.json) under `aiBridge.sharedRelayTools`.

## Complete hosted MCP tool catalog

### Project and scene inspection

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `get_editor_state` Inputs: none | Overview of the open Realot editor: project name, whether the game is playing, selected entity ids, entity count, available component types. |
| `list_entities` Inputs: `limit`: integer | List every entity in the current scene (id, name, tag, active, component types, x/y position). |
| `get_entity` Inputs: **`id`: string (required)** | Full data of one entity: all components with every property. |
| `list_scenes` Inputs: none | List every scene in the project and which one is active. |

### Entities and components

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `create_entity` Inputs: **`name`: string (required)**; `x`: number; `y`: number; `tag`: string; `components`: object | Create an entity. 'components' maps a component type (e.g. SpriteRenderer, Collider2D, Rigidbody2D, Script) to its properties. A Transform is always added. Undoable with undo. Values are validated: wrong types, unknown properties, invalid enum values (e.g. Light.type), out-of-range numbers, bad hex colors and values the engine would silently clamp are rejected with a message listing every problem and the allowed values; nothing is changed on error. |
| `update_component` Inputs: **`id`: string (required)**; **`type`: string (required)**; **`props`: object (required)** | Change properties of an existing component on an entity (only properties the component already has). Use get\_entity first to see them. Values are validated: wrong types, unknown properties, invalid enum values (e.g. Light.type), out-of-range numbers, bad hex colors and values the engine would silently clamp are rejected with a message listing every problem and the allowed values; nothing is changed on error. |
| `add_component` Inputs: **`id`: string (required)**; **`type`: string (required)**; `props`: object | Add a component to an entity. Values are validated: wrong types, unknown properties, invalid enum values (e.g. Light.type), out-of-range numbers, bad hex colors and values the engine would silently clamp are rejected with a message listing every problem and the allowed values; nothing is changed on error. |
| `remove_component` Inputs: **`id`: string (required)**; **`type`: string (required)** | Remove a component (not Transform) from an entity. |
| `delete_entities` Inputs: **`ids`: array (required)** | Delete entities by id (same as pressing Delete in the editor). Undoable. |
| `select_entities` Inputs: **`ids`: array (required)** | Select entities in the editor so the user sees them in the Inspector. |
| `update_entity` Inputs: **`id`: string (required)**; **`patch`: object (required)** | Rename an entity or change its tag, active flag, or hierarchy folder. Use update\_component for Transform and other components. |
| `create_scene` Inputs: `name`: string; `switch`: boolean | Create a new scene (with a Main Camera). Switches to it unless switch=false. |
| `switch_scene` Inputs: **`scene_id`: string (required)** | Make another scene the active one in the editor. |
| `rename_scene` Inputs: **`scene_id`: string (required)**; **`name`: string (required)** | Rename a scene. |
| `delete_scene` Inputs: **`scene_id`: string (required)**; `confirm`: boolean | Delete a scene. Cannot be undone, so the first call only reports what would be deleted; repeat with confirm=true. A project must keep one scene. |
| `duplicate_scene` Inputs: **`scene_id`: string (required)** | Duplicate a scene (deep copy) and add it to the project. Does not switch to it. |

### Scripts, play mode and diagnostics

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `list_scripts` Inputs: none | Names of all scripts in the project. |
| `get_script` Inputs: **`name`: string (required)** | Source code of a script. |
| `write_script` Inputs: **`name`: string (required)**; **`source`: string (required)** | Create or overwrite a script's source code. Entities already using this script get the new code too. Reports syntax errors. |
| `attach_script` Inputs: **`id`: string (required)**; **`scriptName`: string (required)** | Attach an existing script to an entity (adds a Script component). |
| `set_playing` Inputs: **`playing`: boolean (required)** | Start or stop play mode (opens the game in the play window). |
| `get_console` Inputs: `limit`: integer | Recent editor/play console lines (logs, warnings, script errors). |
| `screenshot` Inputs: none | Image of the scene viewport as the user sees it. |
| `undo` Inputs: none | Undo the last editor change. |
| `redo` Inputs: none | Redo the last undone change. |
| `delete_script` Inputs: **`name`: string (required)**; `confirm`: boolean | Delete a script from the project and clear it from objects using it. Cannot be undone, so the first call reports usage; repeat with confirm=true. |
| `set_script_enabled` Inputs: **`id`: string (required)**; **`enabled`: boolean (required)** | Enable or disable the Script component on an entity without removing it. |
| `set_paused` Inputs: **`paused`: boolean (required)** | Pause or resume the running game. The game must be playing (see set\_playing). |

### Assets and uploads

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `list_assets` Inputs: `kind`: string [all, sprite, animation, frame, tile, audio]; `query`: string; `limit`: integer | List imported images and audio without returning binary data, grouped like the editor's Project folders: Sprites, Animation Clips (uploaded animation frames) and Tiles (tileset images), plus Audio. Use the keys in SpriteRenderer, AudioSource, animation clips, and tilesets. |
| `begin_asset_upload` Inputs: **`file_name`: string (required)**; **`mime_type`: string (required)**; **`size_bytes`: integer (required)**; **`purpose`: string [sprite, audio, animation-image, animation-zip, animation-gif, animation-sheet, tileset-sheet, tileset-tile, frame-asset, tile-asset, project-zip] (required)**; `entity_id`: string; `clip_id`: string; `tileset_entity_id`: string; `role`: string; `grid_cols`: integer; `grid_rows`: integer; `group`: string | Start uploading a custom asset: a sprite, audio file, animation source, tileset image, or a loose image for the Animation Clips folder (purpose 'frame-asset') or Tiles folder (purpose 'tile-asset'). Then send sequential base64 chunks with append\_asset\_upload\_chunk and finish with complete\_asset\_upload. The editor must be open and connected. Maximum 20 MiB per file. Purpose 'project-zip' (a .realot project, max 20 MiB) REPLACES the entire open project and asks the person at the editor to confirm. Animation uploads land in the Animation Clips folder; tileset uploads land in the Tiles folder. |
| `append_asset_upload_chunk` Inputs: **`upload_id`: string (required)**; **`chunk_index`: integer (required)**; **`chunk_base64`: string (required)** | Send one base64-encoded binary chunk for an active asset upload. Chunks must be independent base64 strings, sequential from index 0. Use the chunk size returned by begin\_asset\_upload; retrying the same index and data is safe. |
| `complete_asset_upload` Inputs: **`upload_id`: string (required)** | Validate and import all received bytes using the editor's native import pipeline. Call only after every chunk has been accepted. |
| `cancel_asset_upload` Inputs: **`upload_id`: string (required)** | Discard a staged upload before it is imported. |
| `rename_asset` Inputs: **`key`: string (required)**; **`kind`: string [sprite, frame, animation, tile, audio] (required)**; **`name`: string (required)** | Rename an imported sprite, animation frame, tile or audio asset while preserving its key and references. |
| `delete_asset` Inputs: **`key`: string (required)**; **`kind`: string [sprite, frame, animation, tile, audio] (required)**; `confirm`: boolean | Delete an imported asset. If the asset is referenced by scenes or prefabs, the first call reports those references; set confirm=true only when it is acceptable to leave them unresolved. |
| `slice_asset_into_tileset` Inputs: **`entity_id`: string (required)**; **`asset_key`: string (required)** | Cut one existing project image (for example an uploaded sprite) into a 4x4 grid and fill all 16 Tileset slots with the pieces. The pieces are saved in the Tiles folder under the tileset's name. Undoable. |

### Animation

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `list_animations` Inputs: none | List animation clips and ordered frame keys for every entity in the active scene. |
| `create_animation_clip` Inputs: **`entity_id`: string (required)**; `name`: string; `fps`: number; `loop`: boolean | Create an empty animation clip on an entity, adding SpriteAnimation if needed, and open it in the animation editor. |
| `update_animation_clip` Inputs: **`entity_id`: string (required)**; **`clip_id`: string (required)**; **`fields`: object (required)** | Change an animation clip name, frame rate, loop setting, or collider override. Set collider\_override to null to remove the override. |
| `delete_animation_clip` Inputs: **`entity_id`: string (required)**; **`clip_id`: string (required)** | Delete one animation clip from its entity. The remaining clips and frames are preserved. |
| `move_animation_frame` Inputs: **`entity_id`: string (required)**; **`clip_id`: string (required)**; **`from_index`: integer (required)**; **`to_index`: integer (required)** | Reorder an animation frame by moving it from one zero-based position to another. |
| `delete_animation_frame` Inputs: **`entity_id`: string (required)**; **`clip_id`: string (required)**; **`frame_index`: integer (required)** | Remove one zero-based frame position from an animation clip without deleting the underlying imported asset. |
| `add_animation_frames` Inputs: **`entity_id`: string (required)**; **`clip_id`: string (required)**; **`asset_keys`: array (required)**; `index`: integer | Add images that are already in the project (sprites, Animation Clips frames, or Tiles) to an animation clip as frames. Use list\_assets for keys and list\_animations for entity/clip ids. Optional index inserts at that position instead of appending. Undoable. |

### Tilesets and tilemaps

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `list_tilesets` Inputs: none | List tilesets, tile dimensions, and sprite keys assigned to each role. |
| `update_tileset` Inputs: **`entity_id`: string (required)**; **`patch`: object (required)** | Edit a tileset name, tile dimensions, or selected role-to-sprite assignments. Set a slot to null to clear it. |
| `set_tileset_slot` Inputs: **`entity_id`: string (required)**; **`role`: string (required)**; **`asset_key`: string|null (required)** | Put an existing project image (sprite, animation frame or tile) in one slot of a Tileset, or clear the slot with asset\_key null. Roles come from list\_tilesets. |
| `list_tilemaps` Inputs: none | List Tilemap entities, their assigned tileset entity, painted cell count, and up to 500 grid coordinates. |
| `paint_tilemap` Inputs: **`entity_id`: string (required)**; **`mode`: string [paint, erase] (required)**; **`cells`: array (required)** | Paint or erase grid cells on a Tilemap. Coordinates are integer cell columns and rows, not world coordinates. Undoable. |

### Navigation and physics

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `list_navigation_worlds` Inputs: none | List NavWorld2D entities with bounds, cell size, painted cell counts, and navigation settings. |
| `paint_navigation_cells` Inputs: **`entity_id`: string (required)**; **`mode`: string [walkable, blocked, erase\_walkability, area, clear\_area] (required)**; `area_index`: integer; **`cells`: array (required)** | Paint walkable or blocked navigation cells, restore baked walkability, or set/clear navigation area indices. Coordinates are integer grid columns and rows. Undoable. |
| `update_navigation_world` Inputs: **`entity_id`: string (required)**; **`patch`: object (required)** | Edit NavWorld2D bounds, cell size, obstacle threshold, diagonal movement, dynamic mode, or all 16 area costs. Cell changes invalidate the baked runtime cache. |
| `list_navigation_areas` Inputs: none | List the 16 named navigation area slots and their indices. |
| `set_navigation_area_name` Inputs: **`index`: integer (required)**; **`name`: string (required)** | Rename one navigation area slot. Slot 0 is the default Ground area and cannot be cleared. |
| `list_physics_layers` Inputs: none | List all 16 named physics layers and their indices. |
| `set_physics_layer_name` Inputs: **`index`: integer (required)**; **`name`: string (required)** | Rename one of the 16 physics layer slots. Slot 0 is the default layer and cannot be cleared. |
| `set_collider_layer_filter` Inputs: **`entity_id`: string (required)**; **`layer`: integer (required)**; **`collides_with`: array (required)** | Set a Collider2D's physics layer and the layer indices it collides with. Use list\_physics\_layers to map names to indices. |
| `bake_navworld` Inputs: **`id`: string (required)** | Bake a NavWorld2D from the scene's colliders (the editor's Bake button). Reports walkable and blocked cell counts. |

### Tags, folders and prefabs

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `list_tags` Inputs: none | List the project tag registry. |
| `add_tag` Inputs: **`tag`: string (required)** | Add a tag to the registry. |
| `delete_tag` Inputs: **`tag`: string (required)** | Remove a tag from the registry (Untagged cannot be removed). |
| `list_prefabs` Inputs: none | List prefabs in the project. |
| `create_prefab` Inputs: **`id`: string (required)**; `name`: string | Create a prefab from an entity and link that entity to it. |
| `instantiate_prefab` Inputs: **`prefab_id`: string (required)**; `name`: string; `x`: number; `y`: number | Place a new instance of a prefab in the active scene. |
| `rename_prefab` Inputs: **`prefab_id`: string (required)**; **`name`: string (required)** | Rename a prefab. |
| `delete_prefab` Inputs: **`prefab_id`: string (required)**; `confirm`: boolean | Delete a prefab from the catalogue; existing instances become unlinked. First call reports impact; repeat with confirm=true. |
| `list_folders` Inputs: none | List Hierarchy folders in the active scene (id, name, parentId). |
| `create_folder` Inputs: **`name`: string (required)**; `parent_id`: string | Create a Hierarchy folder, optionally nested in another. Put entities in it with update\_entity folderId. |
| `rename_folder` Inputs: **`folder_id`: string (required)**; **`name`: string (required)** | Rename a Hierarchy folder. |
| `move_folder` Inputs: **`folder_id`: string (required)**; `parent_id`: string | Nest a folder inside another folder, or move it to the top level (omit parent\_id). Cycles are refused. |
| `delete_folder` Inputs: **`folder_id`: string (required)** | Delete a folder. Its entities and sub-folders move up one level; nothing inside is deleted. |
| `update_prefab` Inputs: **`id`: string (required)**; `apply_position`: boolean; `apply_rotation`: boolean; `apply_scale`: boolean | Push an instance's current data to its prefab and to every non-overridden instance across all scenes (the editor's Update Prefab). |
| `revert_prefab` Inputs: **`id`: string (required)** | Reset a prefab instance to its prefab's data, discarding overrides. |
| `unpack_prefab` Inputs: **`id`: string (required)** | Unlink an instance from its prefab, keeping its current data. |

### Export and project files

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `save_project` Inputs: none | Save now (browser autosave slot, and the .realot file if one is being kept up to date). |
| `export_game` Inputs: **`format`: string [html, pwa] (required)**; `title`: string; `download`: boolean | Build the game as a standalone HTML5 or PWA ZIP. By default it also downloads the ZIP in the editor's browser; read the bytes with read\_export\_chunk. APK builds are not supported through MCP. |
| `read_export_chunk` Inputs: **`export_id`: string (required)**; **`chunk_index`: integer (required)** | Read one base64 chunk of the last export\_game ZIP. |
| `release_export` Inputs: **`export_id`: string (required)** | Free the memory held by the last export\_game result. |
| `download_project_zip` Inputs: `name`: string; `optimize_assets`: boolean | Save the whole project as a .realot ZIP, downloaded in the editor's browser (File > Save Project without a file handle). |

### Editor controls

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `open_editor_panel` Inputs: **`panel`: string [animation, tileset, physics\_layers, navigation\_areas] (required)**; `entity_id`: string; `clip_id`: string | Open the animation editor, tileset editor, physics-layer panel, or navigation-area panel. Animation and tileset panels need the matching entity\_id. |
| `set_editor_tool` Inputs: **`tool`: string [select, translate, rotate, scale, pan, tile, erase, nav, nav-block, nav-area, path] (required)**; `entity_id`: string | Choose a viewport tool and optionally select its Tilemap, NavWorld2D, or StrokePath entity so the user can continue painting in the editor. |

## Safe and reliable use

- Start with project inspection. Ask the AI to identify the active scene, selected objects and relevant components before it edits anything.
- Use **Read-only** when you only want explanations or an audit.
- Ask the AI to make a small change first, then inspect the result in the editor and test it in Play mode.
- Use undo for supported scene edits. Do not assume every operation—especially script writes, project-file operations or scene-list changes—can be reversed in the same way. Save a project backup before large edits.
- Review generated JavaScript. Project scripts execute as browser page code and are not an isolated security sandbox. Do not run untrusted scripts or import project archives from sources you do not trust.
- Tool results may contain project names, scenes, scripts, assets and Console output. These are sent to the connected AI app; use an AI provider you trust and avoid connecting projects containing secrets or private data.
- Disconnect when finished and keep the private connector URL secret. Use **Make a new private link** if you think the link has been exposed.

## About the included local MCP companion source

The engine archive also contains a Node.js stdio companion under `mcp-bridge/` and an editor integration module under `project/editor/mcp/EditorBridge.js`. In this supplied build, that editor integration's installer is not called by the editor startup path. The local companion is therefore not a supported, ready-to-connect alternative in the packaged editor. Use the built-in shared relay described above. Developers who want a local stdio integration must first wire and test the companion against the editor; its 23 local tool definitions are not the same interface as the 80 tools exposed by the live shared relay.

> **For AI clients and coding agents:** Start with For AI assistants & LLMs , then read the script-module reference and global runtime API when generating game scripts. AI Bridge tools edit the editor; script APIs run inside the game. They are different interfaces.

<!-- page: docs/reference/ai-crawling.html -->
# AI assistants and documentation search

> How people and AI tools can find accurate Realot Studio documentation from the documentation URL alone.

> **One URL is enough to start:** Fetch llms.txt from the documentation root, then query api/search?q=your%20question . The search endpoint returns the closest matching guides and API pages with the correct relative URLs.

## Pages are directly readable

Each guide is static HTML with the full article text, headings, links, tables and code examples already in the page. JavaScript enhances navigation and search; it is not required to retrieve the documentation content. Every guide also has a Markdown twin at the same path with the `.md` suffix.

## Retrieval workflow

1. Start with the documentation URL you were given. Resolve the site's root, preserving a deployment prefix such as a GitHub Pages repository path.
2. Fetch `llms.txt` from that root. It is a compact map of the documentation sections and retrieval process.
3. Send the full question to `api/search?q=...` using URL encoding. The endpoint searches titles, descriptions, headings, keywords and page text, then ranks the closest matches.
4. Read the top results returned by the endpoint. Each result includes a relative `url`, title, section, relevance score and a useful text snippet. Resolve the returned URL against the documentation root; do not construct page paths yourself.
5. For broad questions, fetch `llms-full.txt`. If the endpoint is unavailable, fetch `search-index.json` and perform the same retrieval locally.
6. For exact engine API questions, fetch `api/index.json` and the human-readable [complete script module index](../api/script-modules.html). The JSON lists component scene fields/defaults, all lifecycle callbacks, enum values, all 24 script API modules and their supported member names, plus global API groups.

The [human search page](../../search.html) uses the same ranking behavior. The endpoint is a relevance-ranked documentation search, not a generative AI model: it returns the closest source pages for the assistant to read and use.

## Machine-readable files

| Path from docs root | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `llms.txt` | Compact index with exact discovery and retrieval instructions. |
| `llms-full.txt` | Full documentation text in one Markdown file. |
| `api/search?q=...` | Question-based search endpoint. Returns the closest matching pages, snippets, relevance scores and relative URLs. |
| `search-index.json` | Complete page search records, including content text, headings and keywords; fallback for tools that cannot call the endpoint. |
| `api/index.json` | Source-derived component and script API catalog, including every supported module member name and component field/default. |
| `api/manifest.json` | Catalog metadata and counts. |
| `sitemap.xml` | Absolute page URLs when built with the public documentation origin. |
| `robots.txt` | Crawler access policy. |

## Editor automation

For an assistant that needs to operate the currently open editor, use the [AI Bridge and MCP reference](ai-bridge.html). The bridge tools modify live project data; they are distinct from the gameplay scripting API catalog.

## Use engine source as the ground truth

The component field catalog is extracted from the runtime component constructors. The script module member lists come from each API module's exported allow-list. Human explanations complement these lists but should not be treated as permission to call undocumented engine internals. If an API member is absent from the source-derived allow-list, do not recommend it as supported.

The documentation uses stable, unversioned URLs. Publishing an updated engine and documentation replaces the current reference at those same paths; users do not need a separate documentation version download.

## Publishing requirements

Build with the public documentation origin so canonical links and `sitemap.xml` contain absolute URLs. Keep `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, `search-index.json`, `api/index.json`, the HTML guides and their Markdown copies together at the same site root. Deploy the included `functions/api/search.js` with Cloudflare Pages Functions to enable `/api/search`.

<!-- page: docs/reference/llm-guide.html -->
# Realot Studio reference for AI assistants

> Practical rules for AI assistants that explain, script, debug and extend Realot Studio projects accurately.

## What is Realot Studio?

Realot Studio is a browser-based 2D game engine with a visual editor, an entity/component runtime, JavaScript gameplay scripts, PixiJS rendering and Rapier2D physics. The Hub and editor run as web applications. The hosted build is updated by publishing web files; users do not install a separate engine executable.

## Retrieve the relevant reference first

Given only the documentation homepage URL, fetch `llms.txt` from its root, then send the user question to `api/search?q=...`. Read the closest returned pages; the endpoint supplies their paths, so do not guess URLs. For API questions, also fetch `api/index.json` and the [complete script module member index](../api/script-modules.html). The JSON catalog is generated from source facts and is the authoritative list of supported component fields, enum values and API module members. Read the linked guide for behavior, prerequisites and examples.

## AI Bridge and editor automation

When an MCP-connected assistant needs to inspect or edit the open project, use the [AI Bridge and MCP guide](ai-bridge.html). It lists the current tools, connection requirements and limits. Do not assume the hosted relay is deployed: it requires a Realot operator to configure it. The MCP tool schemas supplied by the live connection are authoritative for parameters.

## Gameplay script model

Inside a script callback, `this` refers to the entity that owns the script. Transform shortcuts such as `this.x` and `this.y` are always available. Component sub-objects such as `this.rigidbody`, `this.sprite` and `this.camera` require their matching components. `this.transform`, `this.state` and `this.myTouch` are available on every entity. Use the [`this` reference](../api/this.html) for the full context model.

## Source and runtime rules

- Use only documented member names in the module allow-lists; unknown member names raise a typed runtime API error. The member index also flags a known allow-list gap: `this.joint.flexibility` is listed but has no working script accessor in the supplied source; set it in the Inspector.
- Check component requirements before suggesting a component-backed API.
- Use `onUpdate(dt)` for frame-time behavior and `onFixedUpdate(dt)` for fixed-step logic.
- Use entity/world coordinates for Transform, mouse/touch world positions, physics hits and navigation waypoints. Screen coordinates are canvas pixels.
- Do not reach into editor implementation files from gameplay scripts. Keep editor-only code and runtime code separate.
- Project scripts execute as page code; imported scripts should be treated as executable content, not as a secure sandbox.

## Editor settings and components

The editor has no single general Settings dialog. Project/backup choices are in File, layer and navigation-area names are in Edit, panel visibility is in Window, and component fields are in the Inspector. The [Editor settings guide](../editor/settings.html) lists all current menu options and stored performance defaults. The [API index](../api/index.html) links all 25 components and their settings.

## Export behavior

- **HTML5:** downloads a standalone web game package.
- **PWA:** adds a manifest and service worker for installation/offline support.
- **Android APK:** the user clicks Export, chooses Android APK, and downloads the built APK when the remote service finishes. The current editor allowance is 3 APK exports in a rolling 14-day period. A failed or cancelled job returns its count. The output is debug-signed, not Play Store production-signed.
- **Desktop:** shown as coming soon in the supplied Export window.

## Project files

The official portable project file uses the `.realot` extension. Users can install Realot Hub as a PWA on a supported desktop browser, then double-click a downloaded `.realot` file to open that project in the editor. Realot can request permission to save changes back to the same file. If PWA file handling is unavailable, users can open the editor and choose **File → Load Project**.


---

<!-- page: docs/api/components/transform.html -->
# Transform

> Realot Studio Transform component reference: fields, script API, behavior and examples.

> **Scope:** This page documents the Transform component in Realot Studio. Runtime fields are serialized scene data; the Script API section lists only members intentionally exposed to game scripts.

> **Where to find it in the editor:** Inspector (right side) → Transform component, automatically present on every GameObject. Use W/E/R toolbar tools for scene manipulation.

## What it does

Position, rotation and scale. Every spatial entity uses a Transform.

> **Component setup & editor tools:** Transform is automatically present on entities. Select an entity in the Hierarchy; its Transform section appears in the Inspector.

## How to add and use Transform

**Editor path:** Select the target entity in the **Hierarchy** (left side) → look at the **Inspector** (right side) → click **Add Component** at the bottom of the Inspector → search for **Transform** → click the component row. The Add Component picker is a centered modal with a search box; it only lists components not already attached.

For components with a dedicated editor tool, the tool is opened or activated from the location described below. Do not assume that adding the component alone activates its editor; some systems require a separate window, panel, or viewport tool.

## Component setup & editor tools

- Select an entity in the Hierarchy; edit Transform fields in the Inspector. Use the Scene viewport transform gizmo to move/rotate/scale visually.

### What you should see after adding it

The component appears as its own section in the Inspector. Its serialized settings are listed in the **Component data** table below. If a field is conditional, it appears only when the relevant mode/type is selected. If a field is a runtime state field (for example grounded or resolved velocity), treat it as read-only diagnostic state unless the API reference explicitly documents it as writable.

### How to read the settings

For every setting below, the documentation distinguishes **type**, **default**, **meaning**, and tuning direction where behavior is known. When a value represents a direction, use the engine's coordinate convention documented in [Coordinate system](../../reference/coordinate-system.html); do not substitute Unity/Godot conventions.

## Component data

| Field | Type | Purpose | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `x` | number | World position X. | `0` |
| `y` | number | World position Y. | `0` |
| `z` | number | Pseudo-3D depth; affects sprite scale only when Camera.enablePseudo3D is enabled. | `0` |
| `rotation` | number | Rotation in degrees around Z. | `0` |
| `scaleX` | number | Horizontal scale multiplier. | `1` |
| `scaleY` | number | Vertical scale multiplier. | `1` |

## Tuning behavior

These are the practical direction-of-change rules for the most important controls on this component.

| Setting | What changing it does |
| --- | --- |
| `x / y` | World position. Increasing X moves right; increasing Y moves down in the engine’s 2D world convention. |
| `rotation` | Degrees clockwise visually in the screen coordinate convention; 0 points along +X for directional/spot light orientation. |
| `scaleX / scaleY` | 1 is native scale; >1 enlarges; 0.5 halves size; negative values mirror the corresponding axis. |

## Script API

| Member | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lookAt(x, y)` | Method | Point the entity toward a world-space point. |
| `position` | Property (read/write) | { x, y } world-space position; read or assign. |
| `rotation` | Property (read/write) | Rotation in degrees. |
| `scale` | Property (read/write) | Exposed by this script module. |
| `translate(dx, dy)` | Method | Move by a delta amount. |

## Examples

```
this.position = { x: 200, y: 120 };
```

```
this.rotation = 45;
```

```
this.translate(50 * time.deltaTime, 0);
```

> **Need the full workflow?:** Components: complete workflow covers adding, configuring, testing, combining, and removing components.

<!-- page: docs/api/components/spriterenderer.html -->
# SpriteRenderer

> Realot Studio SpriteRenderer component reference: fields, script API, behavior and examples.

> **Scope:** This page documents the SpriteRenderer component in Realot Studio. Runtime fields are serialized scene data; the Script API section lists only members intentionally exposed to game scripts.

> **Where to find it in the editor:** Inspector → Add Component → Sprite Renderer; choose or import sprites from bottom Project → Sprites, then assign the Sprite Renderer sprite.

## What it does

Draw a 2D texture sprite for an entity.

> **Component setup & editor tools:** In the Inspector, use the SpriteRenderer section to choose the sprite, then use its visual fields and the Scene viewport to verify the result.

## How to add and use SpriteRenderer

**Editor path:** Select the target entity in the **Hierarchy** (left side) → look at the **Inspector** (right side) → click **Add Component** at the bottom of the Inspector → search for **SpriteRenderer** → click the component row. The Add Component picker is a centered modal with a search box; it only lists components not already attached.

For components with a dedicated editor tool, the tool is opened or activated from the location described below. Do not assume that adding the component alone activates its editor; some systems require a separate window, panel, or viewport tool.

## Component setup & editor tools

- Inspector → SpriteRenderer → sprite field: choose the sprite asset. Use the viewport to see the result. FlipX/FlipY are visual orientation controls; color/opacity change appearance without changing the source asset.

### What you should see after adding it

The component appears as its own section in the Inspector. Its serialized settings are listed in the **Component data** table below. If a field is conditional, it appears only when the relevant mode/type is selected. If a field is a runtime state field (for example grounded or resolved velocity), treat it as read-only diagnostic state unless the API reference explicitly documents it as writable.

### How to read the settings

For every setting below, the documentation distinguishes **type**, **default**, **meaning**, and tuning direction where behavior is known. When a value represents a direction, use the engine's coordinate convention documented in [Coordinate system](../../reference/coordinate-system.html); do not substitute Unity/Godot conventions.

## Component data

| Field | Type | Purpose | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `spriteKey` | nullable value | Asset key for the sprite texture. | `null` |
| `color` | hex color string | Tint color. | `#ffffff` |
| `opacity` | number | Opacity multiplier. | `1` |
| `flipX` | boolean | Mirror horizontally. | `false` |
| `flipY` | boolean | Mirror vertically. | `false` |
| `visualRotation` | number | Visual-only rotation in degrees, added to Transform.rotation when drawing. | `0` |
| `referenceWidth` | nullable value | Optional reference width used by rendering/layout. | `null` |
| `referenceHeight` | nullable value | Optional reference height used by rendering/layout. | `null` |

## Tuning behavior

These are the practical direction-of-change rules for the most important controls on this component.

| Setting | What changing it does |
| --- | --- |
| `opacity` | 0 is invisible; 1 is fully opaque; values between are translucent. |
| `flipX / flipY` | Boolean mirror. Flip X changes left/right without changing the Transform position. |

## Script API

| Member | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `color` | Property (read/write) | Hex tint color. |
| `flipX` | Property (read/write) | Horizontal mirror. |
| `flipY` | Property (read/write) | Vertical mirror. |
| `opacity` | Property (read/write) | The `this.sprite` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `texture` | Property (read/write) | Sprite asset key. |
| `visualRotation` | Property (read/write) | The `this.sprite` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |

## Examples

```
this.sprite.texture = "target";
```

```
this.sprite.flipX = input.keyDown("ArrowLeft");
```

> **Need the full workflow?:** Components: complete workflow covers adding, configuring, testing, combining, and removing components.

# ShapeRenderer

> Realot Studio ShapeRenderer component reference: fields, script API, behavior and examples.

> **Scope:** This page documents the ShapeRenderer component in Realot Studio. Runtime fields are serialized scene data; the Script API section lists only members intentionally exposed to game scripts.

> **Where to find it in the editor:** Create directly from top GameObject → Shape → Square/Circle/Capsule/Triangle, or Inspector → Add Component → Shape Renderer.

## What it does

Draw a procedural 2D shape without requiring a sprite asset.

> **Component setup & editor tools:** Use ShapeRenderer when you want a procedural shape without importing an image.

## How to add and use ShapeRenderer

**Editor path:** Select the target entity in the **Hierarchy** (left side) → look at the **Inspector** (right side) → click **Add Component** at the bottom of the Inspector → search for **ShapeRenderer** → click the component row. The Add Component picker is a centered modal with a search box; it only lists components not already attached.

For components with a dedicated editor tool, the tool is opened or activated from the location described below. Do not assume that adding the component alone activates its editor; some systems require a separate window, panel, or viewport tool.

## Component setup & editor tools

- Inspector → ShapeRenderer: choose the shape type and edit its dimensions. For triangle/freeform shapes, the corresponding viewport gizmo is used when available.

### What you should see after adding it

The component appears as its own section in the Inspector. Its serialized settings are listed in the **Component data** table below. If a field is conditional, it appears only when the relevant mode/type is selected. If a field is a runtime state field (for example grounded or resolved velocity), treat it as read-only diagnostic state unless the API reference explicitly documents it as writable.

### How to read the settings

For every setting below, the documentation distinguishes **type**, **default**, **meaning**, and tuning direction where behavior is known. When a value represents a direction, use the engine's coordinate convention documented in [Coordinate system](../../reference/coordinate-system.html); do not substitute Unity/Godot conventions.

## Component data

| Field | Type | Purpose | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shapeType` | ShapeType enum: Square | Circle | Triangle | Capsule | Square, Circle, Triangle or Capsule. | `Square` |
| `width` | number | Square | `100` |
| `height` | number | Square height. | `100` |
| `radius` | number | Circle | `50` |
| `capsuleHalfHeight` | number | Capsule: a "stadium" shape (rectangle with semicircle caps), same halfHeight/radius convention as Collider2D's capsule so the two stay easy to eyeball-match if a user wants a visual capsule over a capsule collider. | `50` |
| `capsuleRadius` | number | Capsule cap radius. | `30` |
| `trianglePoints` | array | Triangle: 3 points in the entity's LOCAL space (same space Collider2D.trianglePoints uses), user-editable via draggable gizmo handles in the Scene view. | `[{x:-50,y:50}, {x:50,y:50}, {x:0,y:-50}]` |
| `fillColor` | hex color string | Fill color. | `#3a8ede` |
| `visualRotation` | number | Visual-only rotation in degrees, added to Transform.rotation when drawing. | `0` |
| `opacity` | number | Opacity. | `1` |
| `outlineEnabled` | boolean | Enable outline. | `false` |
| `outlineColor` | hex color string | Outline color. | `#ffffff` |
| `outlineWidth` | number | Outline width. | `2` |

## Script API

| Member | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `capsuleHalfHeight` | Property (read/write) | The `this.shape` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `capsuleRadius` | Property (read/write) | The `this.shape` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `fillColor` | Property (read/write) | The `this.shape` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `height` | Property (read/write) | The `this.shape` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `opacity` | Property (read/write) | The `this.shape` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `outlineColor` | Property (read/write) | The `this.shape` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `outlineEnabled` | Property (read/write) | The `this.shape` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `outlineWidth` | Property (read/write) | The `this.shape` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `radius` | Property (read/write) | The `this.shape` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `shapeType` | Property (read/write) | The `this.shape` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `visualRotation` | Property (read/write) | The `this.shape` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `width` | Property (read/write) | The `this.shape` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |

## Examples

```
this.shape.fillColor = "#22c55e";
```

```
this.shape.shapeType = "Circle";
```

```
this.shape.radius = 32;
```

# TextRenderer

> Realot Studio TextRenderer component reference: fields, script API, behavior and examples.

> **Scope:** This page documents the TextRenderer component in Realot Studio. Runtime fields are serialized scene data; the Script API section lists only members intentionally exposed to game scripts.

> **Where to find it in the editor:** Top UI menu → Text, or Inspector → Add Component → Text; screen-space text is authored from the same Inspector component.

## What it does

Render text either in world space or as screen-space UI.

> **Component setup & editor tools:** TextRenderer displays text as a screen/world-space rendering component depending on the entity/camera context.

## How to add and use TextRenderer

**Editor path:** Select the target entity in the **Hierarchy** (left side) → look at the **Inspector** (right side) → click **Add Component** at the bottom of the Inspector → search for **TextRenderer** → click the component row. The Add Component picker is a centered modal with a search box; it only lists components not already attached.

For components with a dedicated editor tool, the tool is opened or activated from the location described below. Do not assume that adding the component alone activates its editor; some systems require a separate window, panel, or viewport tool.

## Component setup & editor tools

- Inspector → TextRenderer: edit the text and presentation properties. For runtime changes, use the documented this.text API.

### What you should see after adding it

The component appears as its own section in the Inspector. Its serialized settings are listed in the **Component data** table below. If a field is conditional, it appears only when the relevant mode/type is selected. If a field is a runtime state field (for example grounded or resolved velocity), treat it as read-only diagnostic state unless the API reference explicitly documents it as writable.

### How to read the settings

For every setting below, the documentation distinguishes **type**, **default**, **meaning**, and tuning direction where behavior is known. When a value represents a direction, use the engine's coordinate convention documented in [Coordinate system](../../reference/coordinate-system.html); do not substitute Unity/Godot conventions.

## Component data

| Field | Type | Purpose | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | string | Displayed text. | `Text` |
| `fontSize` | number | Font size. | `32` |
| `color` | hex color string | Text color. | `#ffffff` |
| `fontFamily` | string | Font family name. | `Arial` |
| `bold` | boolean | Bold text. | `false` |
| `italic` | boolean | Italic text. | `false` |
| `align` | string | "left" | "center" | "right" — multi-line text alignment | `left` |
| `anchorX` | number | 0–1, this text's own pivot point (0.5,0.5 = centered on Transform.x/y, matching a sprite's default anchor) | `0.5` |
| `anchorY` | number | Vertical anchor from 0 to 1. | `0.5` |
| `opacity` | number | Opacity. | `1` |
| `screenSpace` | boolean | see file header — true = fixed UI overlay, false = world-space | `true` |
| `wordWrap` | boolean | Enable wrapping. | `false` |
| `wrapWidth` | number | px — only used while wordWrap is true | `300` |

## Tuning behavior

These are the practical direction-of-change rules for the most important controls on this component.

| Setting | What changing it does |
| --- | --- |
| `fontSize` | Higher = larger text. |
| `anchorX / anchorY` | 0 = top/left pivot, 0.5 = center, 1 = bottom/right pivot for the text block. |
| `wrapWidth` | Only used when wordWrap is enabled; larger width permits longer lines before wrapping. |

## Script API

| Member | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `align` | Property (read/write) | The `this.text` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `anchorX` | Property (read/write) | The `this.text` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `anchorY` | Property (read/write) | Vertical anchor. |
| `bold` | Property (read/write) | Bold toggle. |
| `color` | Property (read/write) | Hex text color. |
| `fontFamily` | Property (read/write) | Font family. |
| `fontSize` | Property (read/write) | Font size. |
| `italic` | Property (read/write) | Italic toggle. |
| `opacity` | Property (read/write) | The `this.text` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `screenSpace` | Property (read/write) | The `this.text` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `value` | Property (read/write) | The `this.text` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `wordWrap` | Property (read/write) | Enable word wrapping. |
| `wrapWidth` | Property (read/write) | The `this.text` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |

## Examples

```
this.text.value = "Score: " + score;
```

```
this.text.screenSpace = true;
```
