<!-- page: docs/api/components/strokepath.html -->
# StrokePath

> Realot Studio StrokePath component reference: fields, script API, behavior and examples.

> **Scope:** This page documents the StrokePath component in Realot Studio. Runtime fields are serialized scene data; the Script API section lists only members intentionally exposed to game scripts.

> **Where to find it in the editor:** Top GameObject → 2D Object → Stroke Path. After a Stroke Path exists, the toolbar exposes Path (P); click empty space to append, drag points, and click segments to insert.

## What it does

A variable-thickness strip along placed points — rivers, cables, roads, conveyor belts or walls — with flat color or textured fill.

> **Component setup & editor tools:** StrokePath creates a drawable strip/path; its editing is performed with the Stroke Path viewport tool/gizmo.

## How to add and use StrokePath

**Editor path:** Select the target entity in the **Hierarchy** (left side) → look at the **Inspector** (right side) → click **Add Component** at the bottom of the Inspector → search for **StrokePath** → click the component row. The Add Component picker is a centered modal with a search box; it only lists components not already attached.

For components with a dedicated editor tool, the tool is opened or activated from the location described below. Do not assume that adding the component alone activates its editor; some systems require a separate window, panel, or viewport tool.

## Component setup & editor tools

- Select an entity with StrokePath → use the Stroke Path viewport tool/gizmo to edit path points. Keep the Inspector open for serialized path/material settings.

### What you should see after adding it

The component appears as its own section in the Inspector. Its serialized settings are listed in the **Component data** table below. If a field is conditional, it appears only when the relevant mode/type is selected. If a field is a runtime state field (for example grounded or resolved velocity), treat it as read-only diagnostic state unless the API reference explicitly documents it as writable.

### How to read the settings

For every setting below, the documentation distinguishes **type**, **default**, **meaning**, and tuning direction where behavior is known. When a value represents a direction, use the engine's coordinate convention documented in [Coordinate system](../../reference/coordinate-system.html); do not substitute Unity/Godot conventions.

## Component data

| Field | Type | Purpose | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `points` | array | Two default points (a minimal, visibly-a-path starting shape) rather than one or zero — a single point has no strip to draw at all, so a StrokePath freshly added via the GameObject menu or Add Component window shows \*something\* immediately instead of an invisible/degenerate result the user has to fix before they can… | `[{x:-100,y:0}, {x:100,y:0}]` |
| `thickness` | number | Strip thickness. | `40` |
| `color` | hex color string | Flat fill color, used when useTexture is false. | `#8a8a8a` |
| `opacity` | number | Opacity. | `1` |
| `useTexture` | boolean | Use an image texture along the path instead of a flat fill. | `false` |
| `textureKey` | nullable value | Logical sprite key, resolved to a PIXI.Texture the same way SpriteRenderer.spriteKey is (see runtime/assets/AssetManager.js resolveTexture) — components never hold PIXI objects directly, for the same "stay serializable" reason SpriteRenderer doesn't. | `null` |
| `textureMode` | StrokePathTextureMode enum: stretch | tile | See StrokePathTextureMode above — STRETCH (fit the whole image to the path, may distort) or TILE (repeat at native size, never stretched). | `stretch` |
| `textureTiling` | number | TILE mode only: how many world units of path length one full texture tile covers lengthwise — e.g. | `100` |
| `textureScale` | number | How many times the texture repeats ACROSS the strip's own thickness (perpendicular to the direction of travel) — kept separate from textureTiling (the lengthwise axis) since a texture like a road stripe or brick run almost always needs a different repeat rate across its width than along its length. | `1` |
| `textureOffset` | number | Slides the texture lengthwise along the path without moving any point — e.g. | `0` |
| `textureFlip` | boolean | Mirrors the texture across the path's own centerline (flips which side is "up") without needing a second, mirrored copy of the source image — handy for a texture that's only authored for one direction of travel. | `false` |
| `textureRotation` | number | Rotates the texture, in degrees, around the center of each tile — independent of every other texture setting above, and applied in TEXTURE space (not world space), so it stays a fixed "printed at an angle on the image" look rather than a rotation that would need to track the path's own direction as it turns. | `0` |
| `jointMode` | StrokePathJointMode enum: sharp | bevel | round | See StrokePathJointMode above — SHARP (hard corner), BEVEL (flat chamfer), or ROUND (filled arc). | `round` |
| `capMode` | StrokePathCapMode enum: none | box | round | See StrokePathCapMode above — NONE (flat stop), BOX (flat, but extended slightly past the tip), or ROUND (half-circle cap). | `round` |
| `smoothing` | number | 0-1. Runs the authored `points` through a Catmull-Rom spline resample BEFORE tessellation, turning the raw straight-segment polyline into a smooth curve — same idea as a spline/curve tool in a 3D package, applied to this 2D strip. | `0` |

## Tuning behavior

These are the practical direction-of-change rules for the most important controls on this component.

| Setting | What changing it does |
| --- | --- |
| `thickness` | Larger values make the strip wider. |
| `textureTiling` | In TILE mode, larger values make each repeated texture cover more path length, so the image repeats less often. |
| `textureScale` | Higher scales the texture; lower makes it smaller/repeated more densely. |
| `textureOffset` | Changing this over time scrolls the texture along the path. |
| `opacity` | 0 invisible, 1 opaque. |

## Script API

| Member | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `addPoint(x, y)` | Method | The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on any entity that has a StrokePath component. |
| `capMode` | Property (read/write) | The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on any entity that has a StrokePath component. |
| `color` | Property (read/write) | The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on any entity that has a StrokePath component. |
| `firstPoint` | Property (read-only) | The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on any entity that has a StrokePath component. |
| `getLength()` | Method | The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on any entity that has a StrokePath component. |
| `getPoint(index)` | Method | The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on any entity that has a StrokePath component. |
| `insertPoint(index, x, y)` | Method | The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on any entity that has a StrokePath component. |
| `jointMode` | Property (read/write) | The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on any entity that has a StrokePath component. |
| `lastPoint` | Property (read-only) | The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on any entity that has a StrokePath component. |
| `localToWorld(localX, localY)` | Method | The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on any entity that has a StrokePath component. |
| `opacity` | Property (read/write) | The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on any entity that has a StrokePath component. |
| `pointCount` | Property (read-only) | The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on any entity that has a StrokePath component. |
| `points` | Property (read/write) | The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on any entity that has a StrokePath component. |
| `removePoint(index)` | Method | The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on any entity that has a StrokePath component. |
| `setPoint(index, x, y)` | Method | The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on any entity that has a StrokePath component. |
| `textureFlip` | Property (read/write) | The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on any entity that has a StrokePath component. |
| `textureKey` | Property (read/write) | The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on any entity that has a StrokePath component. |
| `textureMode` | Property (read/write) | The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on any entity that has a StrokePath component. |
| `textureOffset` | Property (read/write) | The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on any entity that has a StrokePath component. |
| `textureRotation` | Property (read/write) | The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on any entity that has a StrokePath component. |
| `textureScale` | Property (read/write) | The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on any entity that has a StrokePath component. |
| `textureTiling` | Property (read/write) | The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on any entity that has a StrokePath component. |
| `thickness` | Property (read/write) | The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on any entity that has a StrokePath component. |
| `useTexture` | Property (read/write) | The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on any entity that has a StrokePath component. |
| `worldToLocal(worldX, worldY)` | Method | The `this.strokePath` sub-object exposed to user scripts on any entity that has a StrokePath component. |

## Notes & behavior

- Points are placed with the Path tool in the Scene viewport, then adjusted by dragging a point or clicking a segment to insert a new one between two existing points.
- An open polyline (A to B), not a closed loop.
- Reads/writes on this.strokePath.points always operate on a copy, so mutating a returned array can never silently corrupt the live component; assign it back (or use the point methods) to apply a change.

## Examples

```
this.strokePath.addPoint(this.x, this.y);
```

```
this.strokePath.textureOffset += 20 * time.deltaTime; // flowing river/conveyor look
```

> **Need the full workflow?:** Components: complete workflow covers adding, configuring, testing, combining, and removing components.

# SpeechBubble

> Realot Studio SpeechBubble component reference: fields, script API, behavior and examples.

> **Scope:** This page documents the SpeechBubble component in Realot Studio. Runtime fields are serialized scene data; the Script API section lists only members intentionally exposed to game scripts.

> **Where to find it in the editor:** Top UI → Speech Bubble, or Inspector → Add Component → Speech Bubble.

## What it does

Speech bubble UI attached to an entity, useful for dialogue and NPC callouts.

> **Component setup & editor tools:** SpeechBubble provides an in-scene speech presentation attached to an entity.

## How to add and use SpeechBubble

**Editor path:** Select the target entity in the **Hierarchy** (left side) → look at the **Inspector** (right side) → click **Add Component** at the bottom of the Inspector → search for **SpeechBubble** → click the component row. The Add Component picker is a centered modal with a search box; it only lists components not already attached.

For components with a dedicated editor tool, the tool is opened or activated from the location described below. Do not assume that adding the component alone activates its editor; some systems require a separate window, panel, or viewport tool.

## Component setup & editor tools

- Inspector → SpeechBubble: configure its display properties; use the documented SpeechBubble API to change content at runtime.

### What you should see after adding it

The component appears as its own section in the Inspector. Its serialized settings are listed in the **Component data** table below. If a field is conditional, it appears only when the relevant mode/type is selected. If a field is a runtime state field (for example grounded or resolved velocity), treat it as read-only diagnostic state unless the API reference explicitly documents it as writable.

### How to read the settings

For every setting below, the documentation distinguishes **type**, **default**, **meaning**, and tuning direction where behavior is known. When a value represents a direction, use the engine's coordinate convention documented in [Coordinate system](../../reference/coordinate-system.html); do not substitute Unity/Godot conventions.

## Component data

| Field | Type | Purpose | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | string | Current bubble text. | `Hello!` |
| `visible` | boolean | Whether visible. | `false` |
| `backgroundColor` | hex color string | Bubble background. | `#ffffff` |
| `textColor` | hex color string | Text color. | `#111111` |
| `borderColor` | hex color string | Border color. | `#111111` |
| `borderWidth` | number | Border width. | `2` |
| `fontSize` | number | Font size. | `20` |
| `fontFamily` | string | Font family. | `Arial` |
| `padding` | number | px between the text and the bubble's edge | `12` |
| `cornerRadius` | number | Corner radius. | `10` |
| `maxWidth` | number | px — text wraps at this width | `220` |
| `offsetX` | number | px offset from this entity's own position | `0` |
| `offsetY` | number | negative = above the entity's head (typical) | `-60` |
| `tailDirection` | string | "down" | "up" | "left" | "right" | "none" — which edge the pointer triangle sits on, pointing back at the entity | `down` |
| `tailSize` | number | Tail size. | `14` |
| `hideTimer` | number | Auto-hide countdown in seconds, ticked down by SpeechBubbleSystem while visible; 0 or less means "stays visible until hidden manually" (see this.speechBubble.hide()). | `0` |

## Tuning behavior

These are the practical direction-of-change rules for the most important controls on this component.

| Setting | What changing it does |
| --- | --- |
| `maxWidth` | Higher lets a line run longer before wrapping. |
| `offsetY` | Negative values move the bubble upward from the entity in the default screen convention. |
| `padding` | Higher creates more interior space around text. |
| `cornerRadius` | Higher makes corners rounder. |

| `fontFamily` | Property (read/write) | Font family. |
| `fontSize` | Property (read/write) | Font size. |
| `hide()` | Method | The `this.speechBubble` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `maxWidth` | Property (read/write) | The `this.speechBubble` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `offsetX` | Property (read/write) | The `this.speechBubble` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `offsetY` | Property (read/write) | Vertical offset. |
| `padding` | Property (read/write) | Padding. |
| `show(text, duration)` | Method | The `this.speechBubble` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `tailDirection` | Property (read/write) | The `this.speechBubble` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `tailSize` | Property (read/write) | Tail size. |
| `text` | Property (read/write) | The `this.speechBubble` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `textColor` | Property (read/write) | Text color. |
| `visible` | Property (read/write) | The `this.speechBubble` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |


# ChatLog

> Realot Studio ChatLog component reference: fields, script API, behavior and examples.

> **Scope:** This page documents the ChatLog component in Realot Studio. Runtime fields are serialized scene data; the Script API section lists only members intentionally exposed to game scripts.

> **Where to find it in the editor:** Top UI → Chat Log, or Inspector → Add Component → Chat Log.

## What it does

Scrollable-style conversation log component for UI dialogue.

> **Component setup & editor tools:** ChatLog provides a dialogue/log display component intended for scripted text updates.

## How to add and use ChatLog

**Editor path:** Select the target entity in the **Hierarchy** (left side) → look at the **Inspector** (right side) → click **Add Component** at the bottom of the Inspector → search for **ChatLog** → click the component row. The Add Component picker is a centered modal with a search box; it only lists components not already attached.

For components with a dedicated editor tool, the tool is opened or activated from the location described below. Do not assume that adding the component alone activates its editor; some systems require a separate window, panel, or viewport tool.

## Component setup & editor tools

- Inspector → ChatLog: configure the log; use its script-facing API for runtime messages/entries.

### What you should see after adding it

The component appears as its own section in the Inspector. Its serialized settings are listed in the **Component data** table below. If a field is conditional, it appears only when the relevant mode/type is selected. If a field is a runtime state field (for example grounded or resolved velocity), treat it as read-only diagnostic state unless the API reference explicitly documents it as writable.

### How to read the settings

For every setting below, the documentation distinguishes **type**, **default**, **meaning**, and tuning direction where behavior is known. When a value represents a direction, use the engine's coordinate convention documented in [Coordinate system](../../reference/coordinate-system.html); do not substitute Unity/Godot conventions.

## Component data

| Field | Type | Purpose | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `messages` | array | [{ sender, text, senderColor }], oldest first | `[]` |
| `maxMessages` | number | total history kept — oldest dropped once exceeded | `50` |
| `visibleCount` | number | how many of the most recent messages are shown at once | `6` |
| `width` | number | Log width. | `320` |
| `lineHeight` | number | Line height. | `26` |
| `fontSize` | number | Font size. | `16` |
| `fontFamily` | string | Font family. | `Arial` |
| `messageColor` | hex color string | Message color. | `#ffffff` |
| `senderColor` | hex color string | default sender-name color if a message doesn't specify its own | `#ffd700` |
| `backgroundColor` | hex color string | Background. | `#000000` |
| `backgroundOpacity` | number | semi-transparent panel behind the text, typical chat-overlay look | `0.5` |
| `padding` | number | Padding. | `10` |
| `showSender` | boolean | false = just the message text, no "Name: " prefix (good for narration logs) | `true` |
| `screenSpace` | boolean | see TextRenderer.js's file header for the exact meaning — true = fixed UI overlay, false = world-space (e.g. | `true` |
| `visible` | boolean | Visibility. | `true` |

## Tuning behavior

These are the practical direction-of-change rules for the most important controls on this component.

| Setting | What changing it does |
| --- | --- |
| `maxMessages` | Total retained history before oldest messages are dropped. |
| `visibleCount` | How many recent messages are shown at once. |
| `backgroundOpacity` | 0 transparent, 1 opaque. |
| `lineHeight` | Higher creates more vertical spacing between messages. |

## Script API

| Member | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backgroundColor` | Property (read/write) | Background color. |
| `backgroundOpacity` | Property (read/write) | Background opacity. |
| `clear()` | Method | The `this.chat` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `fontFamily` | Property (read/write) | Font family. |
| `fontSize` | Property (read/write) | Font size. |
| `lineHeight` | Property (read/write) | Line height. |
| `maxMessages` | Property (read/write) | Maximum retained messages. |
| `messageColor` | Property (read/write) | Message color. |
| `messages` | Property (read-only) | The `this.chat` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `padding` | Property (read/write) | Padding. |
| `screenSpace` | Property (read/write) | Screen-space mode. |
| `send(sender, text, color)` | Method | The `this.chat` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `senderColor` | Property (read/write) | The `this.chat` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `showSender` | Property (read/write) | The `this.chat` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `visible` | Property (read/write) | Visibility. |
| `visibleCount` | Property (read/write) | Number of visible rows. |
| `width` | Property (read/write) | Panel width. |

## Examples

```
this.chat.send("Guard", "Halt!", "#ef4444");
```

# TextInput

> Realot Studio TextInput component reference: fields, script API, behavior and examples.

> **Scope:** This page documents the TextInput component in Realot Studio. Runtime fields are serialized scene data; the Script API section lists only members intentionally exposed to game scripts.

> **Where to find it in the editor:** Top UI → Message Input, or Inspector → Add Component → Text Input.

## What it does

Interactive text input control driven by the runtime UI system.

> **Component setup & editor tools:** TextInput creates an editable text-entry control and is typically created from GameObject → UI or the Inspector Add Component picker.

## How to add and use TextInput

**Editor path:** Select the target entity in the **Hierarchy** (left side) → look at the **Inspector** (right side) → click **Add Component** at the bottom of the Inspector → search for **TextInput** → click the component row. The Add Component picker is a centered modal with a search box; it only lists components not already attached.

For components with a dedicated editor tool, the tool is opened or activated from the location described below. Do not assume that adding the component alone activates its editor; some systems require a separate window, panel, or viewport tool.

## Component setup & editor tools

- GameObject → UI → Message Input creates a TextInput entity. You can also select an entity → Inspector → Add Component → Text Input.

### What you should see after adding it

The component appears as its own section in the Inspector. Its serialized settings are listed in the **Component data** table below. If a field is conditional, it appears only when the relevant mode/type is selected. If a field is a runtime state field (for example grounded or resolved velocity), treat it as read-only diagnostic state unless the API reference explicitly documents it as writable.

### How to read the settings

For every setting below, the documentation distinguishes **type**, **default**, **meaning**, and tuning direction where behavior is known. When a value represents a direction, use the engine's coordinate convention documented in [Coordinate system](../../reference/coordinate-system.html); do not substitute Unity/Godot conventions.

## Component data

| Field | Type | Purpose | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | string | Current text. |  |
| `placeholder` | string | Placeholder text. | `Type a message...` |
| `maxLength` | number | Maximum characters. | `200` |
| `fontSize` | number | Font size. | `18` |
| `fontFamily` | string | Font family. | `Arial` |
| `textColor` | hex color string | Text color. | `#111111` |
| `placeholderColor` | hex color string | Placeholder color. | `#999999` |
| `backgroundColor` | hex color string | Background. | `#ffffff` |
| `borderColor` | hex color string | Border. | `#888888` |
| `borderWidth` | number | Border width. | `2` |
| `cornerRadius` | number | Corner radius. | `8` |
| `width` | number | Control width. | `260` |
| `height` | number | Control height. | `40` |
| `padding` | number | Horizontal/vertical padding. | `10` |
| `clearOnSubmit` | boolean | empty the field automatically after Enter — typical chat-box behavior | `true` |
| `focused` | boolean | Live state — see the file header for why these live here rather than in TextInputSystem's private state. | `false` |
| `justSubmitted` | boolean | one-frame pulse: true for exactly one frame after Enter is pressed | `false` |

## Tuning behavior

These are the practical direction-of-change rules for the most important controls on this component.

| Setting | What changing it does |
| --- | --- |
| `maxLength` | Hard cap on typed characters. |
| `width / height` | Changes the visual input box size. |
| `borderWidth` | Higher = thicker border. |
| `padding` | Higher moves the text farther from the box edge. |

## Script API

| Member | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backgroundColor` | Property (read/write) | Background color. |
| `borderColor` | Property (read/write) | Border color. |
| `borderWidth` | Property (read/write) | Border width. |
| `clear()` | Method | The `this.textInput` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `clearOnSubmit` | Property (read/write) | The `this.textInput` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `cornerRadius` | Property (read/write) | Corner radius. |
| `focused` | Property (read-only) | The `this.textInput` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `fontFamily` | Property (read/write) | Font family. |
| `fontSize` | Property (read/write) | Font size. |
| `height` | Property (read/write) | Control height. |
| `justSubmitted` | Property (read-only) | The `this.textInput` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `maxLength` | Property (read/write) | Character cap. |
| `padding` | Property (read/write) | Padding. |
| `placeholder` | Property (read/write) | Placeholder. |
| `placeholderColor` | Property (read/write) | Placeholder color. |
| `textColor` | Property (read/write) | Text color. |
| `value` | Property (read/write) | The `this.textInput` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `width` | Property (read/write) | Control width. |

## Examples

```
if (this.textInput.justSubmitted) {
  sendMessage("Chat", "message", this.textInput.value);
  this.textInput.clear();
}
```

# Joystick

> Realot Studio Joystick component reference: fields, script API, behavior and examples.

> **Scope:** This page documents the Joystick component in Realot Studio. Runtime fields are serialized scene data; the Script API section lists only members intentionally exposed to game scripts.

> **Where to find it in the editor:** Top UI → Joystick, or Inspector → Add Component → Joystick.

## What it does

Virtual touch joystick for mobile and pointer-driven control schemes.

> **Component setup & editor tools:** Joystick provides a touch/drag virtual control for mobile-oriented input.

## How to add and use Joystick

**Editor path:** Select the target entity in the **Hierarchy** (left side) → look at the **Inspector** (right side) → click **Add Component** at the bottom of the Inspector → search for **Joystick** → click the component row. The Add Component picker is a centered modal with a search box; it only lists components not already attached.

For components with a dedicated editor tool, the tool is opened or activated from the location described below. Do not assume that adding the component alone activates its editor; some systems require a separate window, panel, or viewport tool.

## Component setup & editor tools

- GameObject → UI → Joystick creates a joystick entity. You can also select an entity → Inspector → Add Component → Joystick.

### What you should see after adding it

The component appears as its own section in the Inspector. Its serialized settings are listed in the **Component data** table below. If a field is conditional, it appears only when the relevant mode/type is selected. If a field is a runtime state field (for example grounded or resolved velocity), treat it as read-only diagnostic state unless the API reference explicitly documents it as writable.

### How to read the settings

For every setting below, the documentation distinguishes **type**, **default**, **meaning**, and tuning direction where behavior is known. When a value represents a direction, use the engine's coordinate convention documented in [Coordinate system](../../reference/coordinate-system.html); do not substitute Unity/Godot conventions.

## Component data

| Field | Type | Purpose | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `positionMode` | JoystickPositionMode enum: Fixed | Dynamic | Fixed or pointer-positioned joystick. | `Fixed` |
| `regionX` | number | Dynamic-mode touch region — the screen-space rectangle (in the same pixel convention Transform.x/y already use for screen-space UI, see TextInput.js's file header) that a press must land inside to claim this joystick. | `0` |
| `regionY` | number | Region Y. | `0` |
| `regionWidth` | number | Region width. | `640` |
| `regionHeight` | number | Region height. | `720` |
| `baseRadius` | number | Visuals | `60` |
| `knobRadius` | number | Knob radius. | `28` |
| `baseColor` | hex color string | Base color. | `#ffffff` |
| `baseOpacity` | number | Base opacity. | `0.25` |
| `knobColor` | hex color string | Knob color. | `#ffffff` |
| `knobOpacity` | number | Knob opacity. | `0.6` |
| `outlineColor` | hex color string | Outline color. | `#ffffff` |
| `outlineWidth` | number | Outline width. | `2` |
| `deadZone` | number | Behavior 0-1: fraction of baseRadius the knob must move before x/y leaves 0 | `0.1` |
| `returnToCenter` | boolean | true = knob snaps back to center on release; false = holds last position | `true` |
| `hideWhenIdle` | boolean | true = invisible until actively being dragged (works in both position modes) | `false` |
| `idleOpacityMultiplier` | number | when hideWhenIdle is false, how much to dim the whole stick while not in use (1 = no dimming) | `0.35` |
| `x` | number | Live state — see the file header for why these live here rather than in JoystickSystem's private state. | `0` |
| `y` | number | -1..1, vertical knob offset (down = positive), after dead zone | `0` |
| `magnitude` | number | 0..1, distance of the knob from center after dead zone | `0` |
| `angle` | number | degrees, 0 = right, 90 = down (screen-space convention, matches Transform.rotation's clockwise-positive sense) | `0` |
| `active` | boolean | true while a finger/pointer is currently dragging this joystick | `false` |
| `baseScreenX` | number | current drawn base center, in screen px — equals Transform.x/y in Fixed mode, or the recentered touch point in Dynamic mode | `0` |
| `baseScreenY` | number | Inspector field stored on this component. | `0` |

## Tuning behavior

These are the practical direction-of-change rules for the most important controls on this component.

| Setting | What changing it does |
| --- | --- |
| `deadZone` | 0 means even tiny stick displacement is reported; increasing it keeps small movements at zero until the knob moves farther. |
| `baseRadius / knobRadius` | Larger values make the on-screen joystick physically larger. |
| `idleOpacityMultiplier` | Lower makes an idle joystick more transparent when hideWhenIdle is false. |
| `returnToCenter` | True snaps back on release; false preserves the last knob position. |

## Script API

| Member | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `active` | Property (read-only) | The `this.joystick` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `angle` | Property (read-only) | The `this.joystick` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `baseColor` | Property (read/write) | Exposed by this script module. |
| `baseOpacity` | Property (read/write) | Exposed by this script module. |
| `baseRadius` | Property (read/write) | Base radius. |
| `deadZone` | Property (read/write) | The `this.joystick` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `hideWhenIdle` | Property (read/write) | The `this.joystick` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `idleOpacityMultiplier` | Property (read/write) | Exposed by this script module. |
| `knobColor` | Property (read/write) | Exposed by this script module. |
| `knobOpacity` | Property (read/write) | Exposed by this script module. |
| `knobRadius` | Property (read/write) | Knob radius. |
| `magnitude` | Property (read-only) | The `this.joystick` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `outlineColor` | Property (read/write) | Exposed by this script module. |
| `outlineWidth` | Property (read/write) | Exposed by this script module. |
| `positionMode` | Property (read/write) | Joystick positioning mode. |
| `regionHeight` | Property (read/write) | Region height. |
| `regionWidth` | Property (read/write) | Region width. |
| `regionX` | Property (read/write) | The `this.joystick` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `regionY` | Property (read/write) | Touch/pointer region Y. |
| `returnToCenter` | Property (read/write) | The `this.joystick` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `x` | Property (read-only) | The `this.joystick` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `y` | Property (read-only) | The `this.joystick` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |

## Examples

```
this.rigidbody.velocityX = this.joystick.x * 250;
```

# Rigidbody2D

> Realot Studio Rigidbody2D component reference: fields, script API, behavior and examples.

> **Scope:** This page documents the Rigidbody2D component in Realot Studio. Runtime fields are serialized scene data; the Script API section lists only members intentionally exposed to game scripts.

> **Where to find it in the editor:** Inspector (right) → Add Component → Rigidbody 2D. Pair with Collider 2D for a colliding body. Edit → Physics Layers… controls named layer slots.

## What it does

2D physics body backed by the engine physics runtime. Dynamic, Kinematic and Static bodies have different script controls.

> **Component setup & editor tools:** Rigidbody2D gives an entity a Rapier 2D body. Collider2D is normally paired with it when physical contact is required.

## How to add and use Rigidbody2D

**Editor path:** Select the target entity in the **Hierarchy** (left side) → look at the **Inspector** (right side) → click **Add Component** at the bottom of the Inspector → search for **Rigidbody2D** → click the component row. The Add Component picker is a centered modal with a search box; it only lists components not already attached.

For components with a dedicated editor tool, the tool is opened or activated from the location described below. Do not assume that adding the component alone activates its editor; some systems require a separate window, panel, or viewport tool.

## Component setup & editor tools

- Select entity → Inspector → Add Component → Rigidbody 2D. After adding it, the Rigidbody2D section exposes body type, gravity/damping, velocity/drive values, rotation locking, and controller/ground state fields.

### What you should see after adding it

The component appears as its own section in the Inspector. Its serialized settings are listed in the **Component data** table below. If a field is conditional, it appears only when the relevant mode/type is selected. If a field is a runtime state field (for example grounded or resolved velocity), treat it as read-only diagnostic state unless the API reference explicitly documents it as writable.

### How to read the settings

For every setting below, the documentation distinguishes **type**, **default**, **meaning**, and tuning direction where behavior is known. When a value represents a direction, use the engine's coordinate convention documented in [Coordinate system](../../reference/coordinate-system.html); do not substitute Unity/Godot conventions.

## Component data

| Field | Type | Purpose | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bodyType` | BodyType enum: Dynamic | Kinematic | Static | Dynamic | Kinematic | Static. | `Dynamic` |
| `simulated` | boolean | Whether the body participates in physics simulation. | `true` |
| `mass` | number | Dynamic-only | `1` |
| `autoMass` | boolean | Inspector field stored on this component. | `true` |
| `gravityScale` | number | Gravity multiplier. | `1` |
| `linearDamping` | number | Linear damping. | `0` |
| `angularDamping` | number | Angular damping. | `0` |
| `lockRotation` | boolean | Dynamic + Kinematic | `false` |
| `velocityX` | number | working velocity — for Dynamic this is read back FROM Rapier each frame (unless driveVelocityX below is set by a controller this same frame); for Kinematic this is the velocity the caller/script sets to drive the body (consumed by PhysicsWorld as a kinematic move). | `0` |
| `velocityY` | number | Y velocity. | `0` |
| `angularVelocity` | number | Angular velocity. | `0` |
| `driveVelocityX` | nullable value | Set (transiently, one frame at a time) by runtime/systems/ControllerSystem.js to drive a DYNAMIC body's horizontal speed via Rapier's setLinvel while leaving the Y axis (and therefore Rapier's own gravity/impulse integration) alone. | `null` |
| `driveVelocityY` | nullable value | Set (transiently, one frame) by ControllerSystem to override a DYNAMIC body's Y velocity this physics step — used both for a one-shot jump kick (Character Controller/Platformer) and for continuous Y drive (Top-Down, which has no gravity to preserve). | `null` |
| `driveAngularVelocity` | nullable value | Set (transiently, one frame) by ControllerSystem to drive a DYNAMIC body's angular velocity (e.g. | `null` |
| `grounded` | boolean | Read-only contact state: written every physics step from Rapier contact manifolds. | `false` |
| `resolvedVelocityX` | number | KINEMATIC-only, read-only: written every physics step with the ACTUAL movement that the kinematic target-motion query resolved after blocking/sliding against obstacles. | `0` |
| `resolvedVelocityY` | number | Inspector field stored on this component. | `0` |
| `pendingForceX` | number | DYNAMIC-only force/impulse queue: pushed by the scripting API's DynamicRigidbodyAPI (see scripting/components/RigidbodyAPI.js) via .addForce()/.addImpulse()/.addTorque() and drained by PhysicsWorld.\_syncEntity every physics step, exactly like driveVelocityX/Y above — plain, serializable data (RULES.txt section 4)… | `0` |
| `pendingForceY` | number | Inspector field stored on this component. | `0` |
| `pendingImpulseX` | number | Inspector field stored on this component. | `0` |
| `pendingImpulseY` | number | Inspector field stored on this component. | `0` |
| `pendingTorque` | number | Inspector field stored on this component. | `0` |
| `pendingAngularImpulse` | number | Inspector field stored on this component. | `0` |

## Tuning behavior

These are the practical direction-of-change rules for the most important controls on this component.

| Setting | What changing it does |
| --- | --- |
| `mass` | Higher mass makes the body harder to accelerate from the same force/impulse. It does not make gravity itself stronger. |
| `gravityScale` | 1 is the normal engine gravity response for Dynamic bodies; 2 doubles it; 0 disables gravity contribution. |
| `linearDamping` | Higher values remove linear velocity faster; 0 leaves the body with no linear damping. |
| `angularDamping` | Higher values remove rotational velocity faster. |

## Automatic mass and force at a point

- `autoMass` (default `true`): a Dynamic body computes its mass from the attached collider geometry and density. Uncheck it in the Inspector to use the `mass` value instead.
- `angularDamping`: resistance to spinning, separate from linear damping.
- `addForceAtPoint(...)` in the script API pushes the body at a world point, so it also creates torque.

## Script API

| Member | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `addAngularImpulse(t)` | Method | The `this.rigidbody` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `addForce(x, y)` | Method | The `this.rigidbody` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `addForceAtPoint(x, y, pointX, pointY)` | Method | The `this.rigidbody` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `addImpulse(x, y)` | Method | The `this.rigidbody` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `addTorque(t)` | Method | The `this.rigidbody` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `angularDamping` | Property (read/write) | Angular damping. |
| `gravityScale` | Property (read/write) | Gravity multiplier. |
| `groundAngle` | Property (read-only) | The `this.rigidbody` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `groundAngleLimit` | Property (read/write) | The `this.rigidbody` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `grounded` | Property (read-only) | The `this.rigidbody` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `isGrounded` | Property (read-only) | The `this.rigidbody` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `isOnCeiling` | Property (read-only) | The `this.rigidbody` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `isOnSlope` | Property (read-only) | The `this.rigidbody` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `isOnWall` | Property (read-only) | The `this.rigidbody` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `linearDamping` | Property (read/write) | Linear damping. |
| `mass` | Property (read/write) | Dynamic mass. |
| `move(dx, dy)` | Method | The `this.rigidbody` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `resolvedVelocity` | Property (read-only) | The `this.rigidbody` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `slopeMinAngle` | Property (read/write) | The `this.rigidbody` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `type` | Property (read/write) | Dynamic | Kinematic | Static; switching type is supported at runtime. |
| `velocity` | Property (read/write) | {x,y} velocity. |
| `velocityX` | Property (read/write) | Horizontal velocity. |
| `velocityY` | Property (read/write) | Vertical velocity. |
| `wallAngleLimit` | Property (read/write) | The `this.rigidbody` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |

## Notes & behavior

- Kinematic-only methods are meaningful for Kinematic bodies; Dynamic-only force methods apply to Dynamic bodies.
- Position assignment through this.x/this.y is treated as a physics teleport target for non-static bodies.

## Examples

```
this.rigidbody.addImpulse(0, -350);
```

```
this.rigidbody.velocityX = 200;
```

```
this.rigidbody.move(100 * time.deltaTime, 0);
```

> **Need the full workflow?:** Components: complete workflow covers adding, configuring, testing, combining, and removing components.

<!-- page: docs/api/components/collider2d.html -->
# Collider2D

> Realot Studio Collider2D component reference: fields, script API, behavior and examples.

> **Scope:** This page documents the Collider2D component in Realot Studio. Runtime fields are serialized scene data; the Script API section lists only members intentionally exposed to game scripts.

> **Where to find it in the editor:** Inspector → Add Component → Collider 2D. One-way platform, trigger, shape, friction, restitution, density, layer and mask settings live here.

## What it does

Physics collision shape and contact filtering. A Collider2D is also required for accurate pointer/touch hit tests.

> **Component setup & editor tools:** Collider2D defines the collision/trigger shape used by the physics system.

## How to add and use Collider2D

**Editor path:** Select the target entity in the **Hierarchy** (left side) → look at the **Inspector** (right side) → click **Add Component** at the bottom of the Inspector → search for **Collider2D** → click the component row. The Add Component picker is a centered modal with a search box; it only lists components not already attached.

For components with a dedicated editor tool, the tool is opened or activated from the location described below. Do not assume that adding the component alone activates its editor; some systems require a separate window, panel, or viewport tool.

## Component setup & editor tools

- Select entity → Inspector → Add Component → Collider 2D. After adding it, edit Shape, dimensions, Offset, Trigger, Friction, Restitution, Density, Layer, and Mask in the Collider2D section. The viewport Collider gizmo shows the collision shape.

### What you should see after adding it

The component appears as its own section in the Inspector. Its serialized settings are listed in the **Component data** table below. If a field is conditional, it appears only when the relevant mode/type is selected. If a field is a runtime state field (for example grounded or resolved velocity), treat it as read-only diagnostic state unless the API reference explicitly documents it as writable.

### How to read the settings

For every setting below, the documentation distinguishes **type**, **default**, **meaning**, and tuning direction where behavior is known. When a value represents a direction, use the engine's coordinate convention documented in [Coordinate system](../../reference/coordinate-system.html); do not substitute Unity/Godot conventions.

## Component data

| Field | Type | Purpose | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shape` | ColliderShape enum: Box | Circle | Capsule | Triangle | Box | Circle | Capsule | Triangle. | `Box` |
| `width` | number | Box width. | `1` |
| `height` | number | Box height. | `1` |
| `radius` | number | Circle radius. | `0.5` |
| `capsuleHalfHeight` | number | Capsule: a "stadium" shape (rectangle with semicircle caps) — matches Rapier's ColliderDesc.capsule(halfHeight, radius), whose principal axis is Y (i.e. | `0.5` |
| `capsuleRadius` | number | Capsule radius. | `0.3` |
| `trianglePoints` | array | Triangle: 3 points in the entity's LOCAL space (same space as offsetX/offsetY), user-editable via 3 draggable gizmo handles. | `[{x:-0.5,y:0.5}, {x:0.5,y:0.5}, {x:0,y:-0.5}]` |
| `offsetX` | number | Local X offset. | `0` |
| `offsetY` | number | Local Y offset. | `0` |
| `rotation` | number | Collider-only rotation, in degrees, applied on top of the entity's own Transform.rotation. | `0` |
| `isTrigger` | boolean | Trigger-only collider. | `false` |
| `isOneWayPlatform` | boolean | One-way platform: solid only when the other body is landing on it from above; a body approaching from below or the side passes straight through, like a Mario/Metroidvania jump-through platform. | `false` |
| `oneWayDirection` | OneWayDirection enum: Up | Down | Inspector field stored on this component. | `Up` |
| `friction` | number | Surface friction. | `0.5` |
| `restitution` | number | Bounciness. | `0` |
| `density` | number | Density. | `1` |
| `layer` | number | Collision layer/mask — inspired by Unity's physics layer matrix. | `0` |
| `mask` | value | Layers this collider can interact with. | `0xFFFF` |

## Tuning behavior

These are the practical direction-of-change rules for the most important controls on this component.

| Setting | What changing it does |
| --- | --- |
| `restitution` | 0 behaves as non-bouncy; increasing it produces more bounce. Keep in a physically sensible range for predictable results. |
| `friction` | Higher values resist sliding more strongly. Lower values let contacts slide more easily. |
| `density` | Affects mass/inertia when the physics world builds the body from colliders; it is not a direct “heaviness” multiplier on gravity. |
| `offsetX / offsetY` | Moves the collider relative to the entity’s pivot; positive X/right and positive Y/down in world-space convention. |

## Script API

| Member | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `capsuleHalfHeight` | Property (read-only) | Capsule half-height. |
| `capsuleRadius` | Property (read-only) | Capsule radius. |
| `density` | Property (read-only) | Density. |
| `friction` | Property (read-only) | Friction. |
| `height` | Property (read-only) | Box height. |
| `isColliding(other)` | Method | The `this.collider` sub-object exposed to user scripts. |
| `isOneWayPlatform` | Property (read-only) | One-way platform flag. |
| `isTrigger` | Property (read/write) | Trigger-only collider. |
| `layer` | Property (read-only) | Layer index 0-15. |
| `mask` | Property (read-only) | 16-bit interaction mask. |
| `offset` | Property (read-only) | {x,y} collider offset. |
| `oneWayDirection` | Property (read/write) | The `this.collider` sub-object exposed to user scripts. |
| `radius` | Property (read-only) | Circle radius. |
| `restitution` | Property (read-only) | Restitution. |
| `rotation` | Property (read/write) | The `this.collider` sub-object exposed to user scripts. |
| `shape` | Property (read-only) | Box | Circle | Capsule | Triangle. |
| `width` | Property (read-only) | Box width. |

## Notes & behavior

- Collision layers use 16 membership layers (0-15). The mask determines which layers the collider can interact with.
- One-way platforms are intended to block from one side while allowing traversal from the non-blocking side.

## Examples

```
this.collider.isTrigger = true;
```

```
this.collider.layer = 2;
```

```
this.collider.mask = 0xFFFF;
```

> **Need the full workflow?:** Components: complete workflow covers adding, configuring, testing, combining, and removing components.

<!-- page: docs/api/components/joint2d.html -->
# Joint2D

> Realot Studio Joint2D component reference: fields, script API, behavior and examples.

> **Scope:** This page documents the Joint2D component in Realot Studio. Runtime fields are serialized scene data; the Script API section lists only members intentionally exposed to game scripts.

> **Where to find it in the editor:** Inspector → Add Component → Joint 2D; choose Fixed/Revolute/Prismatic/Rope/Spring and configure anchors/limits/motor.

## What it does

Connect physics bodies with Fixed, Revolute, Prismatic, Rope or Spring constraints.

> **Component setup & editor tools:** Joint2D constrains one physics body relative to another and requires compatible Rigidbody2D setup.

## How to add and use Joint2D

**Editor path:** Select the target entity in the **Hierarchy** (left side) → look at the **Inspector** (right side) → click **Add Component** at the bottom of the Inspector → search for **Joint2D** → click the component row. The Add Component picker is a centered modal with a search box; it only lists components not already attached.

For components with a dedicated editor tool, the tool is opened or activated from the location described below. Do not assume that adding the component alone activates its editor; some systems require a separate window, panel, or viewport tool.

## Component setup & editor tools

- Select entity → Inspector → Add Component → Joint 2D. Configure the joint from its Inspector section and make sure the connected physics bodies satisfy the joint’s requirements.

### What you should see after adding it

The component appears as its own section in the Inspector. Its serialized settings are listed in the **Component data** table below. If a field is conditional, it appears only when the relevant mode/type is selected. If a field is a runtime state field (for example grounded or resolved velocity), treat it as read-only diagnostic state unless the API reference explicitly documents it as writable.

### How to read the settings

For every setting below, the documentation distinguishes **type**, **default**, **meaning**, and tuning direction where behavior is known. When a value represents a direction, use the engine's coordinate convention documented in [Coordinate system](../../reference/coordinate-system.html); do not substitute Unity/Godot conventions.

## Component data

| Field | Type | Purpose | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `jointType` | JointType2D enum: Fixed | Revolute | Prismatic | Rope | Spring | Fixed | Revolute | Prismatic | Rope | Spring. | `Revolute` |
| `connectedEntityId` | nullable value | null = jointed to a fixed point in the world instead of another body. | `null` |
| `anchor1X` | number | Local-space anchor points, in pixels — see class doc comment. | `0` |
| `anchor1Y` | number | Local anchor Y on this entity. | `0` |
| `anchor2X` | number | Local anchor X on the connected body/world anchor. | `0` |
| `anchor2Y` | number | Local anchor Y on the connected body/world anchor. | `0` |
| `axisX` | number | Prismatic only: slide axis, local to body1. | `1` |
| `axisY` | number | Prismatic axis Y. | `0` |
| `length` | number | Rope: total physical link-path length of the rope. | `100` |
| `stiffness` | number | Spring only. Note these are NOT the small "intuitive" values a spring might use in an SI/meters engine — Rapier computes spring force from anchor distance in METERS (via World.lengthUnit, see PhysicsWorld.js's LENGTH\_UNIT\_PX\_PER\_METER = 100), so at this engine's pixel scale a rest-length-50px displacement is only… | `6000` |
| `damping` | number | Spring damping. | `18` |
| `flexibility` | number | Revolute only: how freely the connected body may rotate. | `100` |
| `segmentCount` | number | Flexible Rope/Spring physical structure. | `18` |
| `ropeMass` | number | Mass per rope/spring segment. | `0.5` |
| `visualEnabled` | boolean | Runtime rope/string visualization. | `true` |
| `visualColor` | hex color string | Joint/rope visual color. | `#c8a66a` |
| `visualThickness` | number | Visual thickness. | `3` |
| `useTexture` | boolean | Optional image texture running along the rope/string instead of a flat color line — same texture/mode vocabulary as StrokePath (see runtime/components/StrokePath.js), so anyone who has textured a StrokePath already recognizes these fields. | `false` |
| `textureKey` | nullable value | Texture asset key. | `null` |
| `textureMode` | string | "stretch": the whole image is squeezed/stretched to fit the rope's current length end-to-end — warps as the rope swings and its chord length changes. | `stretch` |
| `textureTiling` | number | Tiling length. | `32` |
| `textureScale` | number | Texture scale. | `1` |
| `textureOffset` | number | Texture offset. | `0` |
| `textureFlip` | boolean | Flip texture. | `false` |
| `limitsEnabled` | boolean | Revolute + Prismatic: optional min/max limit on the joint's one free coordinate (degrees for Revolute, pixels for Prismatic). | `false` |
| `limitMin` | number | Minimum limit. | `-45` |
| `limitMax` | number | Maximum limit. | `45` |
| `motorEnabled` | boolean | Revolute + Prismatic: optional motor driving that same free coordinate. | `false` |
| `motorSpeed` | number | Motor target speed. | `0` |
| `motorMaxForce` | number | Maximum motor force. | `0` |
| `jointDrag` | number | Revolute-only passive rotational response. | `0` |
| `restStiffness` | number | Inspector field stored on this component. | `0` |
| `breakable` | boolean | Revolute-only structural failure. | `false` |
| `breakForce` | number | Inspector field stored on this component. | `10000` |
| `disableConnectedCollision` | boolean | When enabled, only this joint's two connected entities stop generating contact pairs with one another. | `false` |
| `collideConnected` | value | Legacy scene/script field. | `undefined` |
| `enabled` | boolean | Editor/gizmo convenience only — never read by PhysicsWorld. | `true` |

## Tuning behavior

These are the practical direction-of-change rules for the most important controls on this component.

| Setting | What changing it does |
| --- | --- |
| `length` | For Rope/Spring, higher length increases the rest/maximum link distance depending on the joint type. |
| `stiffness` | For Spring, higher values pull toward the rest length more strongly. |
| `damping` | Higher damping reduces oscillation faster. |
| `segmentCount` | Rope visual/solver subdivision count; higher can look smoother but costs more. |

## Breakable joints and drag

- `breakable` / `breakForce` (Revolute only): when the joint load exceeds `breakForce` the joint snaps apart. Script `joint.breakable` and `joint.breakForce`.
- `jointDrag` and `restStiffness` (Revolute only): drag/damping and the springiness that pulls the joint back to its rest pose.
- `disableConnectedCollision`: stop the two connected bodies from colliding with each other. It replaces the old `collideConnected` field, which is kept only for loading older projects.

> **Script API note::** JointAPI currently lists flexibility in its proxy allow-list, but the script object has no getter or setter for it. Reading it returns undefined , and writing it does not change the component. Set Flexibility (%) in the Inspector.

## Script API

| Member | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor1` | Property (read/write) | {x,y} local anchor on this body. |
| `anchor2` | Property (read/write) | {x,y} local anchor on connected body/world anchor. |
| `axis` | Property (read/write) | The `this.joint` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `breakForce` | Property (read/write) | Exposed by this script module. |
| `breakable` | Property (read/write) | The `this.joint` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `collideConnected` | Property (read/write) | Collision between connected bodies. |
| `connectedEntity` | Property (read/write) | Connected entity context, when one exists. |
| `damping` | Property (read/write) | Spring damping. |
| `disableConnectedCollision` | Property (read/write) | Exposed by this script module. |
| `enabled` | Property (read/write) | The `this.joint` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `flexibility` | Allow-listed but not implemented | The JointAPI allow-list contains this name, but no getter or setter is implemented. Reads return undefined and writes do not update Joint2D.flexibility. Set Flexibility (%) in the Inspector instead. |
| `jointDrag` | Property (read/write) | The `this.joint` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `jointType` | Property (read/write) | Joint type. |
| `length` | Property (read/write) | The `this.joint` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `limitMax` | Property (read/write) | Maximum limit. |
| `limitMin` | Property (read/write) | Minimum limit. |
| `limitsEnabled` | Property (read/write) | The `this.joint` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `motorEnabled` | Property (read/write) | The `this.joint` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `motorMaxForce` | Property (read/write) | Maximum motor force. |
| `motorSpeed` | Property (read/write) | Motor speed. |
| `restStiffness` | Property (read/write) | The `this.joint` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `ropeMass` | Property (read/write) | Rope/spring segment mass. |
| `segmentCount` | Property (read/write) | The `this.joint` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `stiffness` | Property (read/write) | The `this.joint` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `textureFlip` | Property (read/write) | The `this.joint` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `textureKey` | Property (read/write) | The `this.joint` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `textureMode` | Property (read/write) | The `this.joint` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `textureOffset` | Property (read/write) | The `this.joint` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `textureScale` | Property (read/write) | The `this.joint` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `textureTiling` | Property (read/write) | The `this.joint` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `useTexture` | Property (read/write) | The `this.joint` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `visualColor` | Property (read/write) | Visual color. |
| `visualEnabled` | Property (read/write) | Visual enabled. |
| `visualThickness` | Property (read/write) | Visual thickness. |

## Examples

```
this.joint.connectedEntity = findFirst("Target");
```

```
this.joint.jointType = "Spring";
```

# CharacterController

> Realot Studio CharacterController component reference: fields, script API, behavior and examples.

> **Scope:** This page documents the CharacterController component in Realot Studio. Runtime fields are serialized scene data; the Script API section lists only members intentionally exposed to game scripts.

> **Where to find it in the editor:** Inspector → Add Component → Movement Type. Pick Character Controller, Platformer, Top-Down, Car, Follow or Patrol; fields in the Inspector change with the selected mode.

## What it does

High-level movement modes: Character Controller, Platformer, Top-Down, Car, Follow, Patrol and Free.

> **Component setup & editor tools:** CharacterController provides the higher-level movement behaviors such as Platformer, Car, Follow, or Patrol when configured with the required physics components.

## How to add and use CharacterController

**Editor path:** Select the target entity in the **Hierarchy** (left side) → look at the **Inspector** (right side) → click **Add Component** at the bottom of the Inspector → search for **CharacterController** → click the component row. The Add Component picker is a centered modal with a search box; it only lists components not already attached.

For components with a dedicated editor tool, the tool is opened or activated from the location described below. Do not assume that adding the component alone activates its editor; some systems require a separate window, panel, or viewport tool.

## Component setup & editor tools

- Select entity → Inspector → Add Component → Movement Type (CharacterController). Choose the controller type first; the Inspector then exposes the relevant movement fields. Platformer/Car/Follow/Patrol fields are not interchangeable—configure only the group belonging to the selected controller type.

### What you should see after adding it

The component appears as its own section in the Inspector. Its serialized settings are listed in the **Component data** table below. If a field is conditional, it appears only when the relevant mode/type is selected. If a field is a runtime state field (for example grounded or resolved velocity), treat it as read-only diagnostic state unless the API reference explicitly documents it as writable.

### How to read the settings

For every setting below, the documentation distinguishes **type**, **default**, **meaning**, and tuning direction where behavior is known. When a value represents a direction, use the engine's coordinate convention documented in [Coordinate system](../../reference/coordinate-system.html); do not substitute Unity/Godot conventions.

## Component data

| Field | Type | Purpose | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `controllerType` | ControllerType enum: Character Controller | Platformer | Top-Down | Car | Follow | Patrol | Free | Character Controller | Platformer | Top-Down | Car | Follow | Patrol | Free. | `Character Controller` |
| `moveSpeed` | number | Movement (Character / Platformer / Top-Down) px/s | `200` |
| `acceleration` | number | how fast velocity approaches target (higher = snappier) | `20` |
| `airControl` | number | 0-1 multiplier on acceleration while airborne (Platformer only) | `0.5` |
| `canJump` | boolean | Jump (Character Controller + Platformer) | `true` |
| `jumpForce` | number | px/s upward velocity applied on jump | `420` |
| `maxJumps` | number | 1 = no double jump, 2 = double jump, etc. | `1` |
| `useGravity` | boolean | Gravity (Character Controller can toggle it off for e.g. | `true` |
| `gravityScale` | number | Multiplier on gravity's strength for Character Controller/Platformer (same name/semantics as Rigidbody2D.gravityScale on a Dynamic body — 1 = normal, 2 = falls twice as fast, 0.5 = floaty/moon-gravity, 0 = no downward pull at all while still respecting useGravity's on/off switch). | `1` |
| `useDefaultInput` | boolean | Input. For Character/Platformer/Top-Down and Car, this controls the built-in keyboard while script APIs can contribute in the same frame. | `true` |
| `maxSpeed` | number | Car-specific (Car controller only) top forward speed in px/s | `350` |
| `carAcceleration` | number | how fast the car speeds up (px/s^2) | `200` |
| `brakeForce` | number | how fast it brakes / goes into reverse (px/s^2) | `400` |
| `turnSpeed` | number | max turn rate in deg/s (at full speed; scales down at lower speeds) | `150` |
| `driftFactor` | number | 0-1: how much lateral velocity is retained (higher = more slide) | `0.92` |
| `driveTowardArriveDistance` | number | px from the target that counts as "arrived" for | `12` |
| `targetName` | string | Follow-specific (Follow controller only) name of the entity to pursue |  |
| `followSpeed` | number | pursuit speed in px/s | `150` |
| `followDistance` | number | stop when within this many pixels of the target | `5` |
| `patrolDistance` | number | Patrol-specific (Patrol controller only). | `150` |
| `patrolMode` | PatrolMode enum: Platformer | Top-Down | Patrol's own movement scheme — see PatrolMode above. | `Platformer` |
| `patrolAxis` | PatrolAxis enum: Horizontal | Vertical | Which axis a TopDown-mode Patrol walks along — see PatrolAxis above. | `Horizontal` |
| `requestJump` | boolean | Set (transiently, for one ControllerSystem update) by this.controller.simulateJump() (see scripting/components/ ControllerAPI.js) to trigger a jump from script logic — consumed and reset to false by ControllerSystem.js right after reading it, the same one-shot request pattern Rigidbody2D's pendingForceX/Y uses. | `false` |
| `requestMoveX` | nullable value | Set (transiently, for one ControllerSystem update) by this.controller.simulateMove(x, y) (see scripting/components/ ControllerAPI.js) as a script/joystick movement contribution. | `null` |
| `requestMoveY` | nullable value | Inspector field stored on this component. | `null` |
| `requestThrottle` | nullable value | Set (transiently, for one ControllerSystem update) by this.controller.simulateDrive(throttle, steer) (see scripting/ components/ControllerAPI.js), Car-only. | `null` |
| `requestSteer` | nullable value | Inspector field stored on this component. | `null` |
| `requestJoystickX` | nullable value | Set (transiently, for one ControllerSystem update) by this.controller.simulateDriveJoystick(x, y) (see scripting/ components/ControllerAPI.js), Car-only. | `null` |
| `requestJoystickY` | nullable value | Inspector field stored on this component. | `null` |
| `requestDriveTowardX` | nullable value | Set (transiently, for one ControllerSystem update) by this.controller.simulateDriveToward(x, y) (see scripting/ components/ControllerAPI.js), Car-only. | `null` |
| `requestDriveTowardY` | nullable value | Inspector field stored on this component. | `null` |
| `requestFlip` | boolean | Set (transiently, for one ControllerSystem update) by this.controller.flipDirection() (see scripting/components/ ControllerAPI.js), Patrol-only. | `false` |

## Tuning behavior

These are the practical direction-of-change rules for the most important controls on this component.

| Setting | What changing it does |
| --- | --- |
| `moveSpeed` | Higher = faster target movement. |
| `acceleration` | Higher = reaches the requested speed faster; lower = softer/slower ramp. |
| `airControl` | For Platformer, 0 removes horizontal air steering; 1 gives full ground-like acceleration in air. |
| `jumpForce` | Higher = stronger/faster upward launch; lower = shorter jump. |
| `gravityScale` | 1 = normal controller gravity, 0 = no controller gravity; higher magnifies the pull. |

## Script API

| Member | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `acceleration` | Property (read/write) | Acceleration. |
| `airControl` | Property (read/write) | Air-control factor. |
| `brakeForce` | Property (read/write) | Car brake force. |
| `canJump` | Property (read/write) | Whether jumping is available. |
| `controllerType` | Property (read-only) | Read-only movement type. |
| `driftFactor` | Property (read/write) | Car drift factor. |
| `driveTowardArriveDistance` | Property (read/write) | Exposed by this script module. |
| `facingDirection` | Property (read-only) | Current patrol facing direction. |
| `flipDirection()` | Method | Reverse Patrol direction. |
| `followDistance` | Property (read/write) | Follow distance. |
| `followSpeed` | Property (read/write) | Follow speed. |
| `gravityScale` | Property (read/write) | Gravity scale. |
| `groundAngle` | Property (read-only) | Ground angle. |
| `isGrounded` | Property (read-only) | Ground state. |
| `isOnCeiling` | Property (read-only) | Ceiling contact. |
| `isOnSlope` | Property (read-only) | Slope contact. |
| `isOnWall` | Property (read-only) | Wall contact. |
| `jumpForce` | Property (read/write) | Jump force. |
| `maxJumps` | Property (read/write) | Maximum jumps. |
| `maxSpeed` | Property (read/write) | Car maximum speed. |
| `moveSpeed` | Property (read/write) | Movement speed. |
| `patrolAxis` | Property (read/write) | Horizontal | Vertical. |
| `patrolDistance` | Property (read/write) | Patrol distance. |
| `patrolMode` | Property (read/write) | Platformer | Top-Down. |
| `simulateDrive(throttle, steer)` | Method | Drive a Car controller by script. |
| `simulateDriveJoystick(x, y)` | Method | Drive using joystick-style vector input. |
| `simulateDriveToward(x, y)` | Method | Drive toward a world point. |
| `simulateJump()` | Method | Request a jump. |
| `simulateMove(x, y)` | Method | Drive movement by script. |
| `targetName` | Property (read/write) | Follow target name. |
| `turnSpeed` | Property (read/write) | Car turn speed. |
| `useDefaultInput` | Property (read/write) | Built-in input mapping. |
| `useGravity` | Property (read/write) | Gravity toggle. |

## Notes & behavior

- Car-only fields/actions are meaningful for the Car controller. Patrol has its own patrolMode and patrolAxis. Free is script-driven with no built-in input mapping.

## Examples

```
this.controller.simulateMove(input.keyDown("ArrowRight") ? 1 : 0, 0);
```

```
this.controller.simulateJump();
```

# SpriteAnimation

> Realot Studio SpriteAnimation component reference: fields, script API, behavior and examples.

> **Scope:** This page documents the SpriteAnimation component in Realot Studio. Runtime fields are serialized scene data; the Script API section lists only members intentionally exposed to game scripts.

> **Where to find it in the editor:** Inspector → Add Component → Sprite Animation, then use the Animation editor window to create clips/import frames. The Animation editor is an editor window/modal, not the bottom Project panel.

## What it does

Sprite-sheet/clip animation state on a SpriteRenderer.

> **Component setup & editor tools:** SpriteAnimation stores clips and frames and is edited through the Animation Window.

## How to add and use SpriteAnimation

**Editor path:** Select the target entity in the **Hierarchy** (left side) → look at the **Inspector** (right side) → click **Add Component** at the bottom of the Inspector → search for **SpriteAnimation** → click the component row. The Add Component picker is a centered modal with a search box; it only lists components not already attached.

For components with a dedicated editor tool, the tool is opened or activated from the location described below. Do not assume that adding the component alone activates its editor; some systems require a separate window, panel, or viewport tool.

## Component setup & editor tools

- Select entity → Inspector → SpriteAnimation → Open Animation Window. Create/edit clips, frames, FPS, looping, and playback there; use the Inspector for component-level playback state.

### What you should see after adding it

The component appears as its own section in the Inspector. Its serialized settings are listed in the **Component data** table below. If a field is conditional, it appears only when the relevant mode/type is selected. If a field is a runtime state field (for example grounded or resolved velocity), treat it as read-only diagnostic state unless the API reference explicitly documents it as writable.

### How to read the settings

For every setting below, the documentation distinguishes **type**, **default**, **meaning**, and tuning direction where behavior is known. When a value represents a direction, use the engine's coordinate convention documented in [Coordinate system](../../reference/coordinate-system.html); do not substitute Unity/Godot conventions.

## Component data

| Field | Type | Purpose | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clips` | array | @type {AnimationClip[]} | `[]` |
| `currentClipId` | nullable value | @type {string|null} which clip.id is currently selected/playing | `null` |
| `playing` | boolean | whether playback advances automatically every frame (vs. | `true` |
| `speed` | number | playback speed multiplier — 1 = clip's own fps, 2 = double speed, etc. | `1` |
| `currentFrameIndex` | number | --- Simulation state (still plain numbers/strings, not objects — this is per-entity playback progress, same category of field as Rigidbody2D.velocityX: it changes every frame at runtime, but it's still serializable plain data, not a PIXI/Rapier handle). | `0` |
| `frameElapsed` | number | seconds accumulated since the last frame advance | `0` |

## Script API

| Member | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `currentClip` | Property (read-only) | The `this.animator` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `currentFrame` | Property (read/write) | The `this.animator` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `play(clipName)` | Method | The `this.animator` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `playing` | Property (read-only) | The `this.animator` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `speed` | Property (read/write) | The `this.animator` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `stop()` | Method | The `this.animator` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |
| `totalFrames` | Property (read-only) | The `this.animator` sub-object exposed to user scripts (see scripting/ScriptAPI.js). |

## Examples

```
this.animator.play("Run");
```

```
this.animator.speed = 1.5;
```
